nodes.name: TreeCaptureViewModel.kt
nodes.summary: View model for the tree capture camera screen: it pins a GPS location, waits up to 30 seconds for that location before it accepts a photo, and then hands the photo to TreeCapturer and moves the capture flow forward. It also resumes an interrupted session and its sensors after Android kills the app.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a CompletableDeferred as a one-shot gate so that the photo handler can await the location pin with withTimeoutOrNull, and a sealed class hierarchy for the screen actions.

nodes.name: TreeCaptureState
nodes.summary: Immutable UI state of the capture screen: profile photo URL, location progress and availability, tutorial visibility, convergence percentage, and the forced image scaling options read from developer config.

nodes.name: TreeCaptureAction
nodes.summary: Sealed set of user intents for the capture screen: capture a location, report a captured image file, change the bad-GPS dialog state, toggle the capture tutorial, and create fake trees for testing.

nodes.name: TreeCaptureViewModel
nodes.summary: BaseViewModel subclass that drives the capture screen. Its init block resumes an interrupted session and re-enables the step and orientation sensors, starts GPS updates, and loads the tutorial flag and image scaling config.

nodes.name: handleAction
nodes.summary: Dispatches each TreeCaptureAction. It pins the location only once per photo, awaits the pin with a 30 second timeout before it calls setImage and navigates forward, and shows the bad-GPS state when the location is missing or late.

nodes.name: isFirstTrack
nodes.summary: Returns true when the current power user has not yet captured any tree, so the screen shows the capture tutorial on the first track.

nodes.name: TreeCaptureViewModelFactory
nodes.summary: ViewModelProvider factory that opens the capture flow Koin scope and builds a TreeCaptureViewModel with its dependencies resolved from Koin.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Opens the CaptureFlowScopeManager scope and then constructs the TreeCaptureViewModel, so that the capture flow objects exist before the screen uses them.

nodes.name: DeviceOrientation.kt
nodes.summary: Wraps the Android rotation vector sensor: it keeps the latest rotation matrix in memory and lets the capture code freeze a snapshot of it, which TreeCapturer stores as a tree attribute.

nodes.name: DeviceOrientation
nodes.summary: Lifecycle observer that owns the rotation vector sensor listener and the current 4x4 rotation matrix, and exposes an immutable-from-outside rotationMatrixSnapshot for the capture code.

nodes.name: enable
nodes.summary: Registers the orientation listener on the rotation vector sensor at the fastest rate, and only logs a warning when the device has no such sensor.

nodes.name: disable
nodes.summary: Unregisters the rotation vector listener; it also runs on the lifecycle ON_DESTROY event so that the sensor does not keep running after the owner is gone.

nodes.name: takeSnapshotAndDisable
nodes.summary: Copies the current rotation matrix into rotationMatrixSnapshot and then turns the orientation sensor off.

nodes.name: OrientationEventListener
nodes.summary: Inner SensorEventListener that converts each rotation vector event into the shared rotation matrix and ignores accuracy changes.

nodes.name: onSensorChanged
nodes.summary: Converts the rotation vector values of a sensor event into the rotation matrix with SensorManager.getRotationMatrixFromVector and logs the matrix.

nodes.name: StepCounter.kt
nodes.summary: Tracks the hardware step counter and keeps the absolute step count and the count at the last tree capture in session preferences, so the app can record how many steps the grower walked between two trees.
nodes.languageNotes: Kotlin properties with custom getters and private setters read and write SharedPreferences directly, so the step counts survive process death without a separate save call.

nodes.name: StepCounter
nodes.summary: Lifecycle observer that registers a TYPE_STEP_COUNTER listener, persists step counts under session preference keys, and derives deltaSteps as the steps since the previous tree capture.

nodes.name: enable
nodes.summary: Registers the step counter listener, records whether registration worked, and marks that the next sensor reading must become the new baseline so the delta starts at zero.

nodes.name: disable
nodes.summary: Unregisters the step counter listener and clears the registered flag; it also runs on the lifecycle ON_DESTROY event.

nodes.name: snapshotAbsoluteStepCountOnTreeCapture
nodes.summary: Stores the current absolute step count as the count at tree capture, which resets deltaSteps for the next tree.

nodes.name: StepCountEventListener
nodes.summary: Inner SensorEventListener that writes every step counter reading into preferences and sets the baseline on the first reading after enable.

nodes.name: onSensorChanged
nodes.summary: Saves the reported cumulative step count and, on the first reading after enable, snapshots it as the capture baseline before it logs the count and the delta.

nodes.name: TreeCapturer.kt
nodes.summary: Builds the tree record during one capture: it pins a converged GPS location, creates the Tree with the photo, step counts and rotation matrix, keeps every change in PendingTreeStore for process death, and saves the tree through CreateTreeUseCase.

nodes.name: TreeCapturer
nodes.summary: Stateful coordinator of a single tree capture that holds the generated tree UUID, the location convergence, and the current Tree, and mirrors the current Tree into PendingTreeStore so it can be restored.

nodes.name: pinLocation
nodes.summary: Turns on tree capture mode, suspends until the GPS converges or times out, keeps the generated tree UUID, and returns true only when a location coordinate is available, in which case it also keeps the convergence.

nodes.name: setImage
nodes.summary: Creates the Tree from the pinned UUID, the current session ID, the photo path and the mean coordinates, adds step count and rotation matrix attributes, keeps it as pending, and snapshots the step count for the next tree. It throws when the location or the session is missing.

nodes.name: addAttribute
nodes.summary: Adds a key and value attribute to the current Tree, if there is one, and saves the changed tree to the pending store.

nodes.name: setNote
nodes.summary: Replaces the note text of the current Tree with a copy that holds the new note and saves that copy to the pending store.

nodes.name: restorePendingTree
nodes.summary: Loads the tree that was kept before Android killed the app and makes it the current tree, or returns null when nothing was kept.

nodes.name: discardPendingTree
nodes.summary: Forgets the unsaved tree in memory and in the pending store, for when the user leaves the capture flow.

nodes.name: saveTree
nodes.summary: Saves the current tree with CreateTreeUseCase, then clears the in-memory and pending tree; it returns false and keeps the pending tree when there is no tree or the save throws.

nodes.name: CaptureFlowScope.kt
nodes.summary: Manages the Koin scope that lives for one capture flow and holds the per-flow objects such as TreeCapturer and CaptureFlowNavigationController. It can also reopen the scope at a restored screen after process death.

nodes.name: CaptureFlowScopeManager
nodes.summary: Singleton object that opens, closes and exposes the current capture flow Koin scope, and gives access to the scope component and its navigation controller.

nodes.name: open
nodes.summary: Creates a fresh capture flow scope and closes an existing one first with a warning, so that every flow starts with new scoped objects.

nodes.name: restoreAt
nodes.summary: When no scope is open, reopens it after process death, restores the kept tree, and asks the navigation controller to resume at the given route; when the tree or session does not match, it discards the kept tree but leaves the scope open.

nodes.name: getData
nodes.summary: Returns the CaptureFlowScope component from the open scope and throws an IllegalStateException when no scope is open.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the current capture flow scope, if there is one, and forgets it; calling it twice is safe.

nodes.name: CaptureFlowScope
nodes.summary: KoinScopeComponent whose lazily created scope is the anchor for all objects that are scoped to one capture flow.

nodes.name: Convergence.kt
nodes.summary: Computes the mean, variance and standard deviation of a window of GPS fixes for longitude and latitude, first over the full window and then incrementally as the window slides, so the app can tell when the location has settled.
nodes.languageNotes: The sliding window update uses a recursive mean and variance formula from a math.stackexchange answer instead of Welford's cumulative method, because the window drops old samples.

nodes.name: Convergence
nodes.summary: Holds a fixed list of Location samples and the resulting longitude and latitude ConvergenceStats, and offers full and sliding-window recomputation plus standard deviation accessors.

nodes.name: computeSlidingWindowStats
nodes.summary: Returns new ConvergenceStats after one value leaves the window and one new value enters, using an incremental update of the mean and the variance.

nodes.name: computeConvergence
nodes.summary: Computes the initial longitude and latitude statistics over all locations in the window.

nodes.name: computeSlidingWindowConvergence
nodes.summary: Updates the longitude and latitude statistics in place when the oldest location is replaced by a new location.

nodes.name: longitudinalStandardDeviation
nodes.summary: Returns the standard deviation of the longitude samples, or null before any statistics exist.

nodes.name: latitudinalStandardDeviation
nodes.summary: Returns the standard deviation of the latitude samples, or null when the latitude statistics are not computed yet.

nodes.name: computeStats
nodes.summary: Computes the population mean, variance and standard deviation of a list of doubles in two passes.

nodes.name: LocationDataCapturer.kt
nodes.summary: Observes GPS updates, keeps a sliding window of recent fixes during a tree capture to judge location convergence against configured thresholds, and stores every fix of the current session as JSON location data in the database.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Delegates.observable so that convergence observers are only notified when the percentage increases, and a SupervisorJob IO scope for the database inserts that stopGpsUpdates cancels.

nodes.name: LocationDataCapturer
nodes.summary: Central location service that turns tree capture mode on and off, tracks the current and last in-range Convergence, publishes a convergence percentage to observers, and starts or stops GPS updates through LocationUpdateManager.

nodes.name: locationObserver
nodes.summary: LiveData observer that, in tree capture mode, slides the location window, recomputes the Convergence, updates the convergence percentage and status, and for every fix in a session inserts a LocationEntity with serialized LocationData.

nodes.name: isLocationCoordinateAvailable
nodes.summary: Returns true when a converged or a running Convergence exists, which means a usable coordinate is known.

nodes.name: startGpsUpdates
nodes.summary: Starts location updates once and attaches the location observer; when the location permission is missing it leaves updates off so that a later call can start them.

nodes.name: stopGpsUpdates
nodes.summary: On the main thread, removes the location observer, stops location updates, and cancels the pending database insert jobs.

nodes.name: convergence
nodes.summary: Returns the last in-range Convergence or else the running one, and throws an IllegalStateException when called outside tree capture mode.

nodes.name: converge
nodes.summary: Suspends and polls until the convergence status is CONVERGED or the configured timeout passes, in which case it sets the status to TIMED_OUT.

nodes.name: isConvergenceWithinRange
nodes.summary: Returns true when the current convergence status is CONVERGED.

nodes.name: isInTreeCaptureMode
nodes.summary: Tells whether a tree capture is in progress, which is the case while a generated tree UUID exists.

nodes.name: turnOnTreeCaptureMode
nodes.summary: Starts a tree capture by generating a new tree UUID and setting the convergence status to NOT_CONVERGED.

nodes.name: turnOffTreeCaptureMode
nodes.summary: Ends tree capture mode by clearing the tree UUID, both convergences, the location window and the convergence status.

nodes.name: CaptureFlowNavigationController.kt
nodes.summary: Navigation controller for the capture flow that the current organization defines: it moves between capture steps, saves the tree and loops back to the camera after the last step, ends the session when the user leaves, and resumes the flow after process death.

nodes.name: CaptureFlowNavigationController
nodes.summary: FlowNavigationController subclass built from the org's capture flow that owns the step index of one capture flow and coordinates TreeCapturer, SessionTracker, the sensors and GPS while the user moves through it.

nodes.name: navForward
nodes.summary: Advances to the next capture step; past the last step it resets the index, saves the tree, and pops back to the tree capture route on the main thread.

nodes.name: navBackward
nodes.summary: Steps back one screen in the capture flow, or leaves for the dashboard when the flow is already at its first step.

nodes.name: goToDashboard
nodes.summary: Ends the session and navigates to a single dashboard entry, removing the capture screens from the back stack.

nodes.name: goToUserSelect
nodes.summary: Ends the session and replaces the back stack, dashboard included, with the user select screen.

nodes.name: resumeAt
nodes.summary: After process death, points the flow at the given route and restarts the interrupted session, the step counter, orientation and GPS; it returns false and changes nothing when the route or session does not match.

nodes.name: resolveDestinationRoute
nodes.summary: Maps a flow destination to a NavKey: no-arg routes directly, image review with the current tree photo path, and capture with an empty profile URL; it throws for unknown destinations.

nodes.name: endSession
nodes.summary: Discards the pending tree, closes the capture flow and setup scopes, and then in the background ends the session, stops both sensors, stops GPS and turns off tree capture mode.

nodes.name: SensorDiagnosticsTracker.kt
nodes.summary: Collects live GPS, step counter and orientation readings into a StateFlow for the debug sensor overlay, by observing location updates and convergence changes and by polling the sensors every 500 ms.

nodes.name: GpsState
nodes.summary: Overlay state of the GPS section: last coordinates and accuracy, convergence percentage and status, standard deviations against their thresholds, and whether updates run.

nodes.name: StepState
nodes.summary: Overlay state of the step counter section: absolute count, delta since the last tree, sensor availability, and listener status.

nodes.name: OrientationState
nodes.summary: Overlay state of the orientation section: whether a rotation sensor exists and the azimuth, pitch and roll angles in degrees.

nodes.name: SensorDiagnosticsState
nodes.summary: Aggregate overlay state that groups the GPS, step and orientation sub-states.

nodes.name: SensorDiagnosticsTracker
nodes.summary: Diagnostics service that exposes SensorDiagnosticsState as a StateFlow and owns the observers and the polling coroutine that keep it current.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Registers the convergence percentage and location observers and launches a coroutine that refreshes the state every half second.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Cancels polling, removes both observers, and recreates the coroutine scope so the tracker can start again without leftover children.

nodes.name: updateState
nodes.summary: Reads the current convergence, convergence status, GPS update flag, step counts, sensor availability, and orientation angles from the rotation snapshot, and publishes them as one new state.

nodes.name: CaptureFlowTestFixtures.kt
nodes.summary: Shared test fixtures for capture flow view model tests: default and short capture flow destination lists, a sample Tree, and a factory that builds a real CaptureFlowNavigationController over a mocked org repo.

nodes.name: CaptureFlowTestFixtures
nodes.summary: Internal object that holds a fixed photo path, a three-step and a two-step capture flow, and builders for a sample tree and a navigation controller with relaxed sensor mocks.

nodes.name: tree
nodes.summary: Builds a Tree with a fixed UUID, session 1, empty content, fixed mean coordinates, and an optional photo path.

nodes.name: controller
nodes.summary: Builds a real CaptureFlowNavigationController whose mocked OrgRepo returns an org with the given capture flow and whose sensors and session tracker are relaxed mocks.

nodes.summary: Unit tests for TreeCaptureViewModel that cover session and sensor resume on creation, tutorial and image scaling state, single location pinning, the photo-to-navigation path, the bad-GPS paths, and the 30 second location timeout.
nodes.languageNotes: CompletableDeferred gates and kotlinx-coroutines-test virtual time (advanceTimeBy, advanceUntilIdle) let the tests observe the pending and timed-out states deterministically.

nodes.name: TreeCaptureViewModelTest
nodes.summary: JUnit test class for TreeCaptureViewModel with relaxed MockK dependencies, a main dispatcher rule, and virtual time, covering session resume, tutorial, location pinning, photo handling and timeout behavior.

nodes.summary: Initializes the MockK mocks, makes the user repo return the empty fake user, and mocks the CaptureFlowScopeManager object so tests can stub its navigation controller.

nodes.name: tearDown
nodes.summary: Removes the object mock of CaptureFlowScopeManager after each view model test so later tests see the real singleton.

nodes.name: createViewModel
nodes.summary: Builds a TreeCaptureViewModel with the empty profile URL and all relaxed mocks, for tests that do not need custom constructor values.

nodes.name: affected.py
nodes.summary: CLI that picks which end-to-end Test Buddy flows a PR's diff affects, so CI records annotated videos of only the changed screens. It indexes flows by the test tag ids their steps use and Kotlin files by the tags they use, traces each changed file to the nearest screen files, and picks the cheapest flow cut after the screen under a --max cap.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses dataclasses for plain records and regular expressions to scan Kotlin sources instead of a real parser; select() uses the walrus operator to keep only flows that can show a target.

nodes.name: rel
nodes.summary: Converts a path to a forward-slash POSIX string so flow and source paths compare the same way on every OS.

nodes.name: Step
nodes.summary: Dataclass for one top-level flow step: its 1-based index, a shortened first line for the summary, the tag ids and sub-flows it uses (nested ones included), and its cost in steps run.

nodes.name: Flow
nodes.summary: Dataclass for an indexed flow file with its path, name, header tags and parsed steps, plus cost_to for pricing a cut.

nodes.name: cost_to
nodes.summary: Sums the cost of the first n steps of a flow, counting runFlow sub-flows in full, to price running the flow up to a cut point.

nodes.name: without_absent
nodes.summary: Strips comment lines and whole assertNotVisible blocks from a step, because ids a flow asserts are absent say nothing about which screen it is on.

nodes.name: without_comments
nodes.summary: Drops blank and comment lines from a step block so the step's text fits on one line in the summary.

nodes.name: FlowIndex
nodes.summary: Index of every runnable flow under e2e/flows (skipping .ci- copies and inline.yaml) with each step's tag ids and cost, following runFlow into sub-flows with a cache and a cycle guard.

nodes.name: FlowIndex.__init__
nodes.summary: Scans e2e/flows/*.yaml, reads each flow's header tags through flowfile, and stores a Flow with parsed steps keyed by its project-relative path.

nodes.name: _subflow
nodes.summary: Resolves a runFlow target relative to the calling flow and returns its ids, nested sub-flow paths and total cost, memoized per file and guarded against cycles and missing files.

nodes.name: _steps
nodes.summary: Parses a flow's top-level steps into Step records, collecting ids with ID_RE and adding the ids and cost of every sub-flow a step references.

nodes.name: all_ids
nodes.summary: Returns the union of tag ids used by any step of any indexed flow, which CodeIndex uses to keep only tags that some flow can see.

nodes.name: candidates
nodes.summary: Lists the flows allowed to show a changed screen, leaving out flows tagged known-bug because they are expected to fail.

nodes.name: KtFile
nodes.summary: Dataclass for one scanned Kotlin source file: package, plain and star imports, identifier words, TestTags and R references, public declarations, tag constants and tag-building functions.

nodes.name: CodeIndex
nodes.summary: Regex-based index of the app's Kotlin sources that maps files to the flow tag ids they use, finds the users of each file's declarations, detects navigation hubs, and decides which files count as screens a flow can show.

nodes.name: CodeIndex.__init__
nodes.summary: Builds the code index: scans every Kotlin file under app/src/main, maps tag keys to files, credits tags shown through tagged components, marks files that use 10 or more tagged files as hubs, and computes each file's screen ids with overrides applied.

nodes.name: _declared
nodes.summary: Static helper that collects the non-private class, interface and object names plus top-level fun, val, var and typealias names a Kotlin file declares.

nodes.name: _tag_keys
nodes.summary: Maps tag symbols that some flow uses to keys: constants whose value equals a flow id, and TestTags functions whose string prefix matches templated ids (stored as Prefix_*).

nodes.name: uses
nodes.summary: Decides whether a Kotlin file can see and names a given symbol, honoring same-package access, exact imports and star imports, with an owner-qualified form for TestTags members.

nodes.name: users
nodes.summary: Returns, with caching, the files that reference anything the given file declares; this reverse-dependency lookup drives the hop-by-hop tracing.

nodes.name: screens_from
nodes.summary: Breadth-first search from the changed files over users() up to MAX_HOPS, skipping hubs, that returns the nearest specific screen files with the route taken and the hop count.

nodes.name: files_using_resource
nodes.summary: Finds the Kotlin files that reference an Android resource such as R.string.track, so a resource change can be traced to screens.

nodes.name: _screen
nodes.summary: Decides how a flow shows a file: override ids and an 'after' anchor first, then specific tags shown by few files or by one component, else all its own tags, or None.

nodes.name: id_matches
nodes.summary: Checks whether a flow id matches a set of tag keys, exactly or by prefix when a key ends in * and the id is a templated ${...} id.

nodes.name: Change
nodes.summary: Dataclass for one changed path with its git status letter and, for TestTags.kt and values resources, the added and removed diff lines.

nodes.name: Target
nodes.summary: Dataclass for something a changed file needs a flow to show: candidate screen files with their ids, routes from the change, an optional via label or sub-flow, and a priority order.

nodes.name: why
nodes.summary: Builds the reason shown in the PR summary: either the changed sub-flow, or the arrow-joined route from the changed file to the screen with its matching ids.

nodes.name: Pick
nodes.summary: Dataclass for a selected flow with an optional cut step count (None runs it whole) and the reasons listed for it.

nodes.name: short
nodes.summary: Returns the printable base name of a path, which keeps reasons and lists in the PR comment short.

nodes.name: cost
nodes.summary: Prices running a flow up to step n, adding SETUP_COST for flows tagged org-config or dev-tools that need seeding before they run.

nodes.name: show
nodes.summary: Finds where a flow shows a target: the step that runs a changed sub-flow, or the first step on a screen's ids (after an optional anchor) through up to MAX_EXTRA_STEPS more, keeping the cheapest cut.

nodes.name: targets_for
nodes.summary: Sorts each change into targets, whole-flow runs or unmapped entries: deletions and pure renames, sub-flows, top-level flows, TestTags.kt edits by changed tag names, Kotlin sources and Android resources.

nodes.name: resources
nodes.summary: Extracts (kind, name) resource references from a res/ change: names parsed from the changed lines of a values XML file, or the file name for drawables, layouts and the like.

nodes.name: add_code_target
nodes.summary: Traces a change's files to screens with screens_from and appends a Target ordered by hops, or records why nothing in reach can show the change.

nodes.name: fmt_ids
nodes.summary: Formats up to three sorted ids as backticked Markdown, adding an ellipsis when there are more.

nodes.name: load_overrides
nodes.summary: Reads e2e/ci/affected-overrides.json when it exists, which supplies hand-written screen ids and ignore globs.

nodes.name: select
nodes.summary: Core selection: builds the flow and code indexes, drops ignored changes, runs changed flows whole first, then gives each target the flow with the least extra cost (reusing picked flows, and only those at the cap) and widens cuts as needed.

nodes.name: selectors
nodes.summary: Turns picks into run-flows.sh selectors: a bare flow path for a whole run, or path@N for a cut after N steps.

nodes.name: markdown
nodes.summary: Renders the PR comment section that lists flows to run with their step ranges and reasons, flows over the limit, changed screens no flow reaches, and a collapsed list of unmapped files.

nodes.name: printable
nodes.summary: Escapes control characters such as a newline in a file name as \xNN, so one path stays on one Markdown line.

nodes.name: capped
nodes.summary: Truncates a list to MAX_LISTED lines with an 'and N more' tail so the PR comment stays under GitHub's size limit.

nodes.name: as_json
nodes.summary: Serializes a selection result into the JSON report with selectors, per-flow cuts and reasons, skipped flows, unreachable screens and unmapped changes.

nodes.name: git
nodes.summary: Runs a git command in the checkout and returns its stdout, raising when git fails.

nodes.name: changes_from_git
nodes.summary: Parses NUL-separated git diff --name-status -M output between base and head into Change records, and fetches zero-context diff lines for TestTags.kt and values resources.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry that takes --base/--head or --files, runs select, writes optional --json and --md reports, prints the Markdown to stderr and the selectors to stdout.

nodes.name: cut_flow.py
nodes.summary: Small CLI used by run-flows.sh to print a Test Buddy flow truncated after its first N top-level steps, for the flow.yaml@N selectors that affected.py emits; the copy is written beside the original so runFlow paths still resolve.

nodes.name: cut
nodes.summary: Keeps the flow header and the blocks up to the Nth top-level step, counting only step blocks, so comments before the cut stay and comments after the last kept step are dropped.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Checks for a FLOW.yaml argument and a positive N, prints the usage text on bad input, and writes the cut flow to stdout.

nodes.name: flowfile.py
nodes.summary: Shared parser-free splitter for Test Buddy flow YAML, used by step_shots.py, cut_flow.py, affected.py and validating.py so they agree that a step is a '- ' line at column 0 plus its indented lines. It also reads a flow's header tags and offers a has-tag command for run-flows.sh.

nodes.name: split
nodes.summary: Separates the header up to the '---' line from the body and groups the body into blocks: each step with its indented or blank continuation lines, and each other column-0 line on its own.

nodes.name: is_step
nodes.summary: Reports whether a block is a top-level step, which means its first line starts with '- ' at column 0.

nodes.name: steps
nodes.summary: Returns only the top-level step blocks of a flow, discarding the header and standalone comment blocks.

nodes.name: _uncomment
nodes.summary: Removes a trailing # comment from a header line when the # starts the line or follows whitespace.

nodes.name: tags
nodes.summary: Reads the tag set from a flow header in inline list, scalar or block list form, ignoring comments and quotes; callers use it to find known-bug, org-config and dev-tools flows.

nodes.name: join_recording.py
nodes.summary: CLI that merges the split Android screen recording parts tb writes for one flow (recording.mp4, recording-part2.mp4, ...) into one video with an ffmpeg stream copy and one caption file with shifted SRT times. When ffmpeg or ffprobe is missing or the join fails, it keeps the parts apart under the output name.

nodes.name: parts
nodes.summary: Finds recording*.mp4 parts anywhere under the debug folder and orders them by part number, treating the unnumbered file as part 1.

nodes.name: captions_for
nodes.summary: Returns the .srt caption file next to a video part when tb wrote one, else None.

nodes.name: duration
nodes.summary: Measures a video part's length in seconds with ffprobe; the lengths become the caption offsets of later parts.

nodes.name: shift
nodes.summary: Moves every SRT timestamp in a text by a number of seconds, rounding to milliseconds and reformatting as HH:MM:SS,mmm.

nodes.name: join_captions
nodes.summary: Concatenates the caption cues of all parts, renumbering the cues and shifting each part's times by its offset, or returns None when no part has captions.

nodes.name: keep_apart
nodes.summary: Fallback that moves each part and its captions to OUT.mp4 and OUT-partN.mp4 names without joining them.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point that joins the parts through an ffmpeg concat list without re-encoding, writes the merged captions, deletes the parts and the temporary list, and keeps parts apart on any join error.

nodes.name: step_shots.py
nodes.summary: CLI that prints a copy of a Test Buddy flow with a takeScreenshot added after each screen-changing top-level step (or only at the end in end mode), naming each shot after its step so CI can show per-step screenshots.

nodes.name: label
nodes.summary: Builds a screenshot name from a step's command and its id, text, file or visible value, and says whether the step changes the screen (assert and recording commands do not).

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses --mode steps|end and the flow path, then rewrites the flow with step-NN-name screenshots after the wanted steps and always a final step-NN-end shot.

nodes.name: validating.py
nodes.summary: CLI that picks up to --max flows meant to prove a PR's change for the before-and-after job: flows named on the first validates: line of the PR description, then flows the PR adds or edits that are not tagged known-bug. Description words are accepted only as names of existing flows.

nodes.name: named
nodes.summary: Returns up to 20 words from the first validates: line of the PR description, case-insensitive and tolerant of Markdown list or quote prefixes.

nodes.name: changed
nodes.summary: Lists the top-level flow files the PR adds or modifies between base and head with git diff --diff-filter=AM, excluding sub-flows.

nodes.name: pick
nodes.summary: Combines named and changed flows in that order, removing repeats, enforcing the limit, refusing words that are not existing flow names, and skipping changed known-bug flows; returns picks and skipped items with reasons.

nodes.name: markdown
nodes.summary: Renders the 'Before and after' PR comment heading with a table of validating flows and reasons, or a note that no flow shows the change, plus a not-run line.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry that parses --base, --head, --body-file, --max, --root, --json and --md, runs pick, writes the reports, and prints the chosen flow paths on one line.

nodes.name: verdict.py
nodes.summary: CLI that compares each validating flow's run on the base branch's app with its run on the PR's app and gives validated, not-demonstrated, broken or inconclusive. It writes verdict.json and verdict.md and exits 1 when a flow is broken.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Reads a run folder's summary.json into a dict of flows by name, returning an empty dict when the file is missing or malformed.

nodes.name: side
nodes.summary: Reduces one run of a flow to what the PR comment needs: status, seconds, first error line, whether setup ran, the video and the last two screenshots, with paths relative to the output folder.

nodes.name: judge
nodes.summary: Applies the 2x2 rule: inconclusive when either side did not run, validated for fail then pass, not-demonstrated for pass and pass, otherwise broken with a reason.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point that loads both sides, reads before-missing.txt, judges every flow, writes verdict.json with counts and the base SHA, renders the Markdown table with errors, and sets the exit status.

nodes.name: grade.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic grader for one outcome run of the pr-validating-flow skill eval: it reads the agent's git diff, PR_DESCRIPTION.md, stream-json transcripts and the CI verdict.json, and emits pass, fail or undecided checks for a flow case or a fallback case. It also works as a CLI that prints each check and the scored total.
nodes.languageNotes: Checks use a tri-state pass value (True, False, None), so a check that cannot be decided yet, such as a missing CI verdict, drops out of the score instead of counting as a failure.

nodes.name: git
nodes.summary: Runs a git command against the given repository with check=True and returns its captured stdout; it is the shared subprocess wrapper for every diff inspection in the grader.

nodes.name: diff_names
nodes.summary: Lists the file paths changed since the base commit with git diff --name-only and a diff-filter (added, modified, deleted), splitting the NUL-separated output into a list.

nodes.name: named_flows
nodes.summary: Finds the first validates: line in a PR description and returns the flow names it lists, stripping an optional e2e/flows/ prefix and .yaml suffix the same way the CI's validating-flow reader does.

nodes.name: tags
nodes.summary: Extracts the inline tags list from a Maestro flow's YAML header with a regex, so the grader can spot new flows tagged known-bug or org-config.

nodes.name: removed_assertions
nodes.summary: Returns the assertion lines (assert*, extendedWaitUntil, visible, notVisible) that a zero-context diff shows as removed from an existing flow file, which catches an agent that weakens old flows.

nodes.name: app_smells
nodes.summary: Scans lines added under app/src/main for test-only hacks such as Thread.sleep, delay(, isRunningTest or TestHook and returns each hit cut to 120 characters, as a heuristic sign that the agent bent app code for a test.

nodes.name: transcript_facts
nodes.summary: Parses stream-json agent transcripts, skipping malformed lines, and collects Skill tool names plus all tool inputs to report the skills loaded, whether the agent loaded the pr-validating-flow skill, and whether it used the external tb skill.

nodes.name: grade
nodes.summary: Core rubric of the eval: it gathers the diff, description and transcript facts, records the checks common to both kinds (description written, app code changed, old assertions intact, no test-only app code), then adds flow-kind checks (new flow named on validates:, not known-bug, org flows listed in run-org.sh, CI verdict validated) or fallback-kind checks (no flow claimed, test added and named). It returns the checks with the added and claimed flows and the changed tests.

nodes.name: score
nodes.summary: Counts the passed checks among those that are scored and decided (pass is not None) and returns the (passed, total) pair that serves as the run's score.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line entry of the grader: parses --repo, --base, --kind, an optional --verdict file, repeated --transcript and --json, runs grade, optionally writes the JSON result, prints PASS, FAIL or -- for each check with the score, and always exits 0.

nodes.name: run_outcome.py
nodes.summary: Driver for the outcome eval of the pr-validating-flow skill: it builds a pre-fix base commit for each case and arm (skill or baseline), runs a headless Claude agent on the issue in a fresh repository, can push the branch to CI for a before/after flow verdict and feed it back for a second round, and grades every round with grade.py plus model-judged checks. A report subcommand tabulates all stored runs.
nodes.languageNotes: Prompt templates and judge rubrics live as module-level triple-quoted strings filled with str.format, and the CLI uses argparse subparsers to dispatch run, report and list.

nodes.name: sh
nodes.summary: Thin subprocess wrapper that turns every argument into a string and runs the command with captured text output, plus an optional working directory, environment, timeout and check flag.

nodes.name: git
nodes.summary: Runs git through sh with the eval checkout root as the default working directory and returns stripped stdout; the harness uses it for worktrees, refs, fetches and commits.

nodes.name: cases
nodes.summary: Loads cases.json next to the script and returns the eval cases as a dictionary keyed by case id.

nodes.name: make_base
nodes.summary: Builds the base commit for one case and arm in a temporary detached worktree: it starts at the fix's parent or a given base, lays this branch's CI files over it, adds or removes the skill and its pointer files by arm, deletes the files that reveal the answer and scrubs lines that name them, then commits and stores the sha under refs/skill-eval/base.

nodes.name: agent_env
nodes.summary: Prepares the agent's process environment: it writes a gh stub that always fails, puts it first on PATH, and drops GH_*, GITHUB_* and CLAUDECODE variables so the agent works without GitHub tooling.

nodes.name: claude
nodes.summary: Runs one headless claude -p turn with a fixed tool allowlist, an optional model override and optional session resume, writes the stream-json transcript to a file under a timeout, then returns the result event with the session id.

nodes.name: commit_all
nodes.summary: Stages and commits whatever the agent left uncommitted in its repository under a skill-eval identity, and tolerates the case where nothing changed.

nodes.name: run_ci
nodes.summary: Fetches the agent's branch into the checkout, pushes it to origin and runs e2e/ci/cloud-flows.sh in validate mode to test the named flows on the base app and on the agent's app. It returns the parsed verdict.json and a markdown report with console tails of failed sides, or None and an error tail when the run stops early.

nodes.name: judge
nodes.summary: Asks a tool-less claude instance one of the JUDGES rubrics (handles_not_demonstrated, fallback_is_honest, before_fails_for_the_bug) about the given material, parses its one-line JSON answer into a scored judge check, and returns an undecided check if parsing fails.

nodes.name: grade_round
nodes.summary: Grades one round with grade.grade, then appends model-judged checks: fallback honesty for fallback cases, and for a validated flow whether its before-run failed at the point where the bug shows. It stores the recomputed score on the result.

nodes.name: cmd_run
nodes.summary: Implements the run subcommand: it prepares the run folder, base commit and fresh repository, then for each round prompts the agent (with the issue first, later with real CI, simulated not-demonstrated or no-validating-flow feedback), commits, grades, adds the reaction checks in simulated mode, and writes result.json and a diff patch. It stops once the flow is validated or no feedback remains.

nodes.name: cmd_report
nodes.summary: Implements the report subcommand: it reads every result.json in the work folder and prints a markdown table per case and arm with round-1 and final scores, the failed scored checks (judge checks marked) and the CI verdict detail.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line entry of the outcome eval with run, report and list subcommands; it creates the work folder, dispatches to cmd_run or cmd_report, and for list prints the id, kind and reference of each case.

nodes.name: test_grade.py
nodes.summary: unittest suite for grade.py that builds throwaway git repositories with flow YAML, app code and PR descriptions, then asserts which checks pass for a good flow PR, an honest fallback, and cheats such as removed assertions or test-only delays.

nodes.name: GradeTest
nodes.summary: unittest TestCase that keeps a temporary git repository with small git, write and commit helpers, and exercises grade.grade and grade.transcript_facts across good, cheating and fallback scenarios.

nodes.name: setUp
nodes.summary: Creates a temporary git repository seeded with an old settings flow, an e2e/run-org.sh listing and a minimal Kotlin class, and records its first commit as the grading base.

nodes.name: checks
nodes.summary: Commits the current fixture state, runs grade.grade for the given kind, verdict and transcripts, and returns a map from check id to pass value for short assertions.

nodes.name: test_a_good_flow_pr
nodes.summary: Verifies that an app fix plus a new flow named on the validates: line with a validated CI verdict passes every flow check, while the org-config listing check stays undecided.

nodes.name: test_a_flow_that_passes_on_both_apps_is_not_validated
nodes.summary: Checks that a CI verdict of not-demonstrated, meaning the flow also passes on the base app, makes the ci_verdict_validated check fail.

nodes.name: test_no_flow_and_no_line
nodes.summary: Asserts that a flow-kind PR with an app fix but no new flow and no validates: line fails the new-flow, validates-line and CI-verdict checks.

nodes.name: test_cheats_are_caught
nodes.summary: Confirms that removing an old assertion, adding delay() to app code, tagging the new flow known-bug and adding an org-config flow missing from run-org.sh each make their own check fail.

nodes.name: test_an_honest_fallback
nodes.summary: Verifies that a fallback PR with an app fix, a new unit test named in the description and the phrase no validating flow passes all fallback checks.

nodes.name: test_a_flow_pushed_onto_a_no_symptom_bug_fails
nodes.summary: Ensures that in a fallback case, adding a flow and claiming it on validates: without adding a test fails both no_flow_claimed_as_proof and test_added.

nodes.name: test_transcript_facts
nodes.summary: Feeds a synthetic stream-json transcript with a malformed line, a non-dict message, a Skill call and a Bash read of the tb skill file, and asserts that transcript_facts detects both the pr-validating-flow skill and tb skill usage.

nodes.name: action.yml
nodes.summary: Composite GitHub Action that builds the APK for one variant. It can decode the signing keystore, computes the version code as baseVersionCode from app/build.gradle plus the workflow run number (release builds keep the base number), and runs the matching Gradle assemble task.
nodes.languageNotes: The variant name is capitalized with sed (\u) to form the Gradle task name such as assembleBeta, and the computed offset reaches Gradle as the -Ptreetracker.versionCodeOffset project property. A composite action exposes a step output to its caller through its own outputs block.

nodes.name: action.yml
nodes.summary: Small composite GitHub Action that makes the Gradle wrapper executable and runs the release unit tests (testReleaseUnitTest) with stack traces. It expects the caller to have set up the JDK and the keys file first.

nodes.name: action.yml
nodes.summary: Composite GitHub Action that installs the Temurin JDK 25 with the Gradle cache turned on, then calls the setup-property-file action to write the API keys file, with dummy keys when the caller asks for them.
nodes.languageNotes: A composite action can call another local action with a relative uses: path, which here chains JDK setup and keys file generation into one reusable step.

nodes.name: action.yml
nodes.summary: Composite GitHub Action that writes treetracker.keys.properties, the file of backend client ids and S3 identity pool ids that app/build.gradle loads. It writes placeholder values in dummy mode and otherwise copies the values from environment variables that the calling job maps from repository secrets.

nodes.name: android-e2e.yml
nodes.summary: Required PR check that builds the Test Buddy (tb) CLI at a pinned commit and the debug app, then boots an API 35 emulator with emulated front and back cameras and runs every e2e flow through e2e/run.sh. A failed flow step makes tb exit non-zero, which fails the check.
nodes.languageNotes: The booted AVD is saved once with actions/cache under a key that names the camera setup, and the test run passes -no-snapshot-save so the cached snapshot stays clean for later runs.

nodes.name: build.yml
nodes.summary: Reusable workflow (workflow_call) that checks out a chosen ref, sets up the build environment, builds the requested APK variant with the build-apk action, and uploads it as an app-<variant> artifact. It decodes the keystore only for release and prerelease and returns the version code as a workflow output.
nodes.languageNotes: Secrets are declared as optional workflow_call secrets and mapped to job-level env vars, so callers can pass them with secrets: inherit.

nodes.name: create-release-branch.yml
nodes.summary: Manually started workflow that cuts a new release branch. It checks that the input is an X.Y.Z version, that it is greater than every existing release/X.Y.Z branch on origin and not already taken, then creates release/<version> from master and pushes it.
nodes.languageNotes: The version comparison uses sort -V on the existing branch suffixes, which orders dotted numbers numerically instead of as text.

nodes.name: deploy-firebase-beta.yml
nodes.summary: Manually started deployment that builds the beta or dev variant from a chosen branch through build.yml, then downloads the APK and ships it to a Firebase App Distribution tester group with release notes. It picks the Firebase app id that matches the variant's package; a Slack notification job stays commented out.

nodes.name: deploy-play-store.yml
nodes.summary: Manual workflow that builds the signed release APK through build.yml and uploads it to the production track of Google Play for the org.greenstand.android.TreeTracker package.

nodes.name: e2e-affected.yml
nodes.summary: Non-required PR workflow that picks the e2e flows a PR affects with e2e/ci/affected.py (at most 6) and the flows that should prove the change with e2e/ci/validating.py (at most 3), then runs them as annotated videos through flow-runner-job.yml. Validating flows run on the merge-base app and on the PR app to get a verdict, and the results go to one updatable PR comment and a marked before/after block in the PR description; fork PRs run only when a maintainer dispatches the workflow with the reviewed commit sha.
nodes.languageNotes: The comment job is a JavaScript actions/github-script program with small helpers (text, noMentions, safePath, media, sideCell) that build Markdown tables from summary.json and verdict.json. The multi-line table output uses the name<<DELIMITER heredoc form of $GITHUB_OUTPUT.

nodes.name: flow-runner-job.yml
nodes.summary: Reusable workflow at the core of the flow runner: it builds or restores the tb CLI, builds the debug app (and, for validating flows, a base app at before_ref in a separate git worktree), and runs the selected flows on a cached emulator through e2e/ci/run-job.sh. Afterwards it uploads the results, force-pushes them as one commit to a flow-results/ branch, deletes result branches idle for 14 days, and fails for a failed flow or a lost recording.
nodes.languageNotes: The runner script's exit status is written to a file inside the emulator step, so the always() steps can publish results before the last step fails the job; status 3 means every flow passed but a requested video was not saved.

nodes.name: flow-runner-pr.yml
nodes.summary: PR entry point to the flow runner. It starts from the run-flows label (flows from a run-flows: line in the PR description), from a /run-flows comment by a repo member, or with a smoke test when the PR changes the runner itself, parses selectors and options (--video, --api, --screenshots), calls flow-runner-job.yml, and keeps one summary comment on the PR up to date.
nodes.languageNotes: Cheap if: filters on the event payload run before any job starts, so ordinary comments and description edits do not take a runner.

nodes.name: flow-runner.yml
nodes.summary: Manual workflow_dispatch wrapper around flow-runner-job.yml that exposes every runner option (flow selectors, inline flow YAML, ref, API level, screenshots, video, annotation, validating flows) and grants the contents: write token that pushing results needs. It is made for Claude Code cloud sessions, which have no emulator.

nodes.name: pull_request.yml
nodes.summary: Main PR CI with three parallel jobs on JDK 25, each with a dummy keys file: ktlint and detekt code analysis, unit tests followed by a debug APK build, and Roborazzi screenshot verification that uploads the recorded screenshots.

nodes.name: require-pr-media.yml
nodes.summary: pull_request_target check that reads the PR description for a video (file extension, video tag, GitHub attachment or a common video host) and, unless the PR has a non-UI label or ticked checkbox, an embedded screenshot. It keeps one comment that tags the author with what is missing and fails the status check until the media is present.

nodes.name: skill-tests.yml
nodes.summary: Fast PR workflow, filtered to changes in skills, e2e CI code, flows, workflows and agent docs, that runs pure Python unit tests: the pr-validating-flow skill eval tests and the e2e/ci tests for the PR description block, cloud-flows.sh and flow validation. It needs no emulator, model or secrets.

nodes.name: tb-screen-tour.yml
nodes.summary: Manual workflow with a two-entry matrix (master's app code as the base and this branch's app) that walks the debug app's screens with e2e/tour/tour.sh on a Pixel 6 API 35 emulator. It records the screen in 170-second chunks, joins them with ffmpeg, and uploads each tour as an artifact.
nodes.languageNotes: screenrecord stops after at most 180 seconds, so a background shell loop restarts it until a stop file appears, and ffmpeg's concat demuxer joins the parts without re-encoding.

nodes.name: test.yml
nodes.summary: Reusable workflow (workflow_call) that sets up the build environment, with dummy keys by default, runs the release unit tests through the run-tests composite action, and deletes the generated keys file afterwards.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Explains the two re-runnable evals of the pr-validating-flow skill: a trigger eval that checks whether a session loads the skill only for fix or feature PRs, and an outcome eval that replays six real bugs with and without the skill and grades the agent's PR by code checks, the CI emulator before/after verdict and two model-judged checks. It also gives the run commands, the case table, every graded check and the limits of what the eval can prove.

nodes.name: cases.json
nodes.summary: Defines the six outcome-eval cases that run_outcome.py replays: four 'flow' cases based on the parent of a merged fix commit, where the right answer is a new validating e2e flow, and two 'fallback' cases on a fixed base commit, where the right answer is a unit test plus an honest 'no validating flow'. Each case names its issue text, the reference PR, and the files removed or scrubbed from the base so that the answer is not given away.

nodes.name: trigger.json
nodes.summary: Holds the 20 labeled prompts of the trigger eval: 10 fix or feature requests that must make a session load the pr-validating-flow skill, and 10 near misses (a docs edit, a CI pin bump, a pure refactor, test-only work, emulator seeding, a flow run, a review, a diagnosis and code questions) that must not.

nodes.name: 1416.md
nodes.summary: Eval copy of issue #1416 with the answer hints cut: deleting a user from Settings in airplane mode crashes with an AmazonClientException after the user is already removed locally, because UserSelectViewModel.deleteUser calls MessagesRepo.syncMessages() and its messageUploader.uploadMessages() call sits outside the try/catch. It gives exact signup and add-user steps with test phone numbers.

nodes.name: 1418.md
nodes.summary: Eval copy of issue #1418: when Android kills the process on the Add org step, reopening from recents crashes with 'CaptureSetupScope not open', because Navigation 3 restores Add org while the capture setup scope lived only in memory and AddOrgViewModel reads it in init. The offline repro kills the debug app with adb shell am kill.

nodes.name: 1436.md
nodes.summary: Eval copy of issue #1436, a timing race with no on-screen symptom: SettingsViewModel clears the power-user flag on logout only through its cached state.powerUser, so a logout confirmed before the Room query returns leaves power_user set and the splash screen signs the next person in as the previous power user.

nodes.name: 1442.md
nodes.summary: Eval copy of issue #1442: the org-configured setup steps (session note, wallet select, add wallet) call CaptureSetupNavigationController.navForward without DoubleTapGuard, so the second tap of a double tap lands on the next screen's Next and skips a step, for example the session note straight into capture. The repro seeds an org with e2e/seed-org.sh.

nodes.name: 1447.md
nodes.summary: Eval copy of issue #1447: in an org whose setup flow has a session note or wallet select step, process death on session note, wallet select or add wallet crashes on reopen, because SessionNoteViewModel, WalletSelectViewModel and AddWalletViewModel read the in-memory capture setup scope in init. It notes that Add org had the same crash and got its own fix.

nodes.name: 1448.md
nodes.summary: Eval copy of issue #1448, a state bug with no visible symptom: Settings > Delete account reuses UserSelectViewModel, whose SelectUser action makes the picked user current in Preferences and in CaptureSetupData, and DeleteUser removes the row without a reset of either value, so both keep pointing at a deleted user.

nodes.name: PR_DESCRIPTION.md
nodes.summary: PR description that the baseline agent (no skill) wrote for #1416: it catches and logs a failed syncMessages() in UserSelectViewModel.deleteUser and keeps MessagesRepo throwing because SyncDataUseCase relies on it. Instead of a new flow, it adds 'Account Deleted' assertions to the existing settings-delete-user and settings-delete-admin flows and names those two on its validates line.

nodes.name: ci-r1-verdict.md
nodes.summary: Round-one CI before/after table for the baseline #1416 run: both edited flows, settings-delete-user and settings-delete-admin, failed on the base app at the 'Account Deleted' DialogTitle assertion and passed on the agent's app, so CI marks both as validated.

nodes.name: result.json
nodes.summary: Graded record of the baseline arm on case 1416-delete-user-offline: one round, 14 turns, about 1.90 USD, score 6 of 9. CI validated both claimed flows, but new_flow_added and validates_line_names_new_flow failed because the agent edited existing flows instead of adding one, and the transcript shows neither this skill nor Test Buddy's skill.

nodes.name: PR_DESCRIPTION.md
nodes.summary: PR description that the skill-arm agent wrote for #1416: it follows the PR template checklist, catches the failed syncMessages() in UserSelectViewModel.deleteUser, and adds a new settings-delete-user-offline flow that its validates line names. It explains why the known-bug flows E7 and E8 stay unedited (an edited flow counts as a validating flow and would read as not demonstrating the change) and what the 'before' run must show.

nodes.name: ci-r1-verdict.md
nodes.summary: Round-one CI verdict for the skill-arm #1416 run: the one new flow, settings-delete-user-offline, failed on the base app because the 'Account Deleted' dialog title never became visible and passed on the fixed app, so it is validated.

nodes.name: result.json
nodes.summary: Graded record of the skill arm on case 1416-delete-user-offline: a full 10 of 10 in one round (17 turns, about 2.63 USD). The new flow was added, named on the validates line, not tagged known-bug and validated by CI, the judge confirmed the 'before' run failed at the missing dialog, and the transcript shows both pr-validating-flow and Test Buddy's skill in use.

nodes.name: PR_DESCRIPTION.md
nodes.summary: PR description that the baseline agent wrote for #1418: it saves a CaptureSetupSnapshot (user id, wallet, session note, org name) with the activity state, lets Root reopen the capture setup scope before it shows the restored back stack, and lets Host drop user-dependent setup steps when no user can be restored. It lists three new tests and the new flow sad-process-death-add-org, but it has no validates line.

nodes.name: ci-r1-verdict.md
nodes.summary: Round-one CI verdict for the baseline #1418 run: the agent's new sad-process-death-add-org flow failed on the base app at an OrgNameField visibility assertion and passed on the agent's app, so CI marks it as validated.

nodes.name: result.json
nodes.summary: Graded record of the baseline arm on case 1418-process-death-add-org: 8 of 10 in one round (27 turns, about 4.10 USD). The new flow was added and validated by CI, but the description had no validates line and Test Buddy's skill was not used; the judge accepted the OrgNameField failure but noted that the error text does not say which of two waits failed.

nodes.name: PR_DESCRIPTION.md
nodes.summary: PR description written by the with-skill agent in the outcome eval for issue #1418, where reopening the app on Add org after process death crashed with `CaptureSetupScope not open`. It explains the fix (a new CaptureSetupStore that saves the picked user, wallet, note and org name, a CaptureSetupRestorer that Root calls before Host shows the back stack, and a pop-back fallback), names sad-process-death-add-org on its `validates:` line and admits that nothing was built or run locally.

nodes.name: ci-r1-verdict.md
nodes.summary: CI before-and-after verdict for the with-skill run of case 1418: the new flow sad-process-death-add-org failed on the base app and passed on the agent's app, so it is marked validated. The base-app failure was the Maestro assertion that OrgNameField is visible after the relaunch.

nodes.name: result.json
nodes.summary: Graded result record of the with-skill arm of case 1418-process-death-add-org (one round, 23 turns, about 3.32 USD on claude-fable-5-2). It scores 9 of 10: all scored checks pass, including the CI verdict and the judged before_fails_for_the_bug, except used_tb_skill, because the agent wrote the flow without reading Test Buddy's skill; org_flow_listed_in_run_org stays undecided since this is not an org case.

nodes.name: PR_DESCRIPTION.md
nodes.summary: PR description from the baseline (no skill) agent for issue #1442, where the second tap of a double tap on a capture setup Next lands on the next screen's Next and skips the session note. It puts DoubleTapGuard.modifier and an injectable guard on SessionNoteScreen, WalletSelectScreen and AddWalletScreen, adds screen UI tests and the flow org-session-note-double-tap seeded through run-org.sh, and says only the e2e/ci Python tests (58) were run.

nodes.name: ci-r1-verdict.md
nodes.summary: CI verdict for the baseline run of case 1442: the flow org-session-note-double-tap is validated, because it failed on the base app at the assertion that SessionNoteField is visible (the note was skipped) and passed on the PR's app.

nodes.name: result.json
nodes.summary: Graded result record of the baseline arm of case 1442-double-tap-session-note: 10 of 11 scored checks pass in one round (16 turns, about 2.28 USD). The only failed scored check is used_tb_skill; the agent never loaded pr-validating-flow, yet it added a new org flow listed in run-org.sh and three screen UI tests, and got a validated CI verdict.

nodes.name: PR_DESCRIPTION.md
nodes.summary: PR description from the with-skill agent for issue #1442 that wraps SessionNoteScreen, WalletSelectScreen and AddWalletScreen in a Box carrying the DoubleTapGuard modifier, so a Next pressed within the double-tap timeout of the opening navigation is dropped. It adds the flow org-double-tap-session-note (C6) to run-org.sh, explains why no Robolectric test was added (the test clock advances 1 s per read) and describes what a failing 'before' run should look like.

nodes.name: ci-r1-verdict.md
nodes.summary: CI verdict for the with-skill run of case 1442: org-double-tap-session-note fails on the base app because SessionNoteField is not visible after the double tap, and passes on the PR's app, so the flow counts as validated proof of the fix.

nodes.name: result.json
nodes.summary: Graded result record of the with-skill arm of case 1442-double-tap-session-note, a full 11 of 11 in one round (14 turns, about 1.92 USD). It shows that the agent loaded pr-validating-flow and Test Buddy's skill, changed only the three screen files, listed no test files, and that the judge accepted the base-app failure as the bug's symptom.

nodes.name: PR_DESCRIPTION.md
nodes.summary: PR description from the baseline agent for issue #1447, a `CaptureSetupScope not open` crash when the app reopens on session note, wallet select or add wallet after process death. Its fix keeps the user id, note, wallet and org name in preferences through a new CaptureSetupRestorer, lets the three ViewModels reopen the scope and reload the user, holds Next and Back meanwhile, exits to the Dashboard through LeaveLostSetupEffect, and tabulates the restored state of each screen.

nodes.name: ci-r1-verdict.md
nodes.summary: CI verdict for the baseline run of case 1447 that covers three new flows, all validated. On the base app, org-process-death-session-note failed on SessionNoteField, org-process-death-wallet-select on the user button UserButton_5551230001, and org-process-death-add-wallet on WalletNameField.

nodes.name: result.json
nodes.summary: Graded result record of the baseline arm of case 1447-process-death-session-note: 10 of 11 in one round, the costliest run of this group (33 turns, about 4.89 USD). It lists nine test files and three added flows that CI validated; used_tb_skill failed, and the judge noted that the error text cannot tell the pre-kill assertion from the post-kill wait.

nodes.name: PR_DESCRIPTION.md
nodes.summary: PR description from the with-skill agent for issue #1447 that injects a new CaptureSetupRestorer into SessionNoteViewModel, WalletSelectViewModel and AddWalletViewModel to reopen the setup scope and reload the saved user after process death, with a `restoring` hold and a `setupLost` exit to the Dashboard through SetupLostEffect. It states that typed text and picked wallets are not restored, leaves AddOrgViewModel's own restore alone, and lists the expected before and after results of its three validating flows.

nodes.name: ci-r1-verdict.md
nodes.summary: CI verdict for the with-skill run of case 1447: the three process-death flows are validated. Their base-app failures are SessionNoteField, OrangeAddButton (wallet select) and WalletNameField not visible after the relaunch, the same waits the PR description predicted.

nodes.name: result.json
nodes.summary: Graded result record of the with-skill arm of case 1447-process-death-session-note: 11 of 11 in one round (30 turns, about 4.24 USD). It records that the agent loaded both pr-validating-flow and Test Buddy's skill, lists nine test files including SetupProcessDeathUiTest, and shows all three flows validated by CI.

nodes.name: beta_testing_bug.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub issue form for testers who hit a bug in the version 2.2 beta. It requires the build number, device, Android version, reproduction steps, expected and actual behavior, plus dropdowns for frequency, severity (blocker to cosmetic) and network condition (Wi-Fi, mobile data, offline, intermittent), and asks for the app's shared logs.
nodes.languageNotes: GitHub issue forms use a YAML `body` list of typed fields (input, textarea, dropdown); `validations.required` blocks submission until a field is filled, and `render: shell` shows pasted logs as a code block.

nodes.name: bug_report.yml
nodes.summary: General-purpose GitHub bug report form that tags new issues with the bug and triage labels. It requires a description, reproduction steps, expected behavior, device and Android OS version, and leaves screenshots, app version and extra context optional.

nodes.name: feature.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub issue form for a fully specified roadmap feature that is ready to build. It requires a summary, user stories in the 'As a ..., I want ..., so that ...' shape, functional requirements, an acceptance-criteria checklist and a target version, with optional design, technical notes and dependency fields.

nodes.name: feature_request.yml
nodes.summary: Lightweight GitHub form for anyone to suggest a new idea, labeled feature-request and triage. It asks for the underlying problem and the wanted solution, and optionally for alternatives considered and other context.

nodes.name: tech_debt.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub issue form for recording code-base tech debt, labeled tech-debt and triage. Reporters must describe the debt, explain its impact (for example on performance or maintenance), and pick an urgency of high, medium or low.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: Root agent instructions file (titled AGENTS.md) that requires a numbered docs/tasks/task_{id} folder for every unit of work and a before/after end-to-end flow with annotated videos for each fix or feature PR. It then acts as the table of contents for the docs tree, grouped into getting started, product, engineering, testing and release, collaboration, and process.

nodes.name: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
nodes.summary: Contributor Covenant 1.4 code of conduct for the project, listing expected and unacceptable behavior, the maintainers' right to remove contributions or ban contributors, and the rule that incidents are reported confidentially to the project team by email.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Project landing page that explains the app as the field data collection tool of the Treetracker pipeline and covers setup (getting the treetracker.keys.properties file, using the dev variant). It also describes QC releases through Firebase App Distribution (manual beta builds and a currently disabled GitHub Actions flow), Fastlane installation, Play Store listing tasks, and where to find contribution guidance and the project board.

nodes.name: TD.md
nodes.summary: Short tech-debt note that lists eleven detekt rule names with active flags, mostly rules switched off such as ComplexInterface, TooManyFunctions and EmptyCatchBlock. It is written as flat, unindented YAML-like lines, and its StringLiteralDuplication flag (true) differs from the value in detekt.yml.

nodes.name: build.gradle
nodes.summary: Root Gradle build script that puts the Android, Kotlin, Compose compiler, serialization, KSP, Google services, Crashlytics, Roborazzi and lint plugins on the classpath through version catalog aliases. For every subproject it sets placeholder API key properties, applies ktlint (skipping generated code), detekt with the shared detekt.yml, and Spotless with a copyright license header, and it registers a root clean task.
nodes.languageNotes: Groovy DSL with the legacy buildscript classpath block, but plugin coordinates come from the gradle/libs.versions.toml version catalog (libs.* accessors) instead of hard-coded versions.

nodes.name: codeAnalysis.sh
nodes.summary: Developer helper that runs the formatters first (spotlessApply, ktlintFormat) and then the checkers (ktlintCheck, detekt) in one Gradle wrapper invocation, failing fast under strict bash mode so local code matches the CI lint gates.

nodes.name: decrypt_secret.sh
nodes.summary: Four-line shell helper that uses GPG in batch mode to decrypt secret_properties.enc into treetracker.keys.properties, taking the passphrase from the SECRET_PROP_PWD environment variable. No workflow in the repository calls it; CI now writes the same keys file through the setup-property-file composite action.

nodes.name: detekt.yml
nodes.summary: Detekt static analysis rule set for the Kotlin code, layered on the default config, that turns off most documentation and complexity rules but keeps LargeClass (600 lines), method overloading limits, empty-block, exception, potential-bug and many style checks. Test sources are excluded from most naming and size rules, and ForbiddenComment blocks FIXME and STOPSHIP markers.
nodes.languageNotes: The FunctionNaming pattern accepts backtick-quoted names (common in Kotlin test methods) and ignores functions annotated with @Composable, which use PascalCase by Compose convention.

nodes.name: gradle.properties
nodes.summary: Project-wide Gradle and Android Gradle Plugin flags: official Kotlin code style, AndroidX, a 4 GB daemon heap, all warnings shown, transitive R classes and non-final resource IDs kept on the old behavior, and unit tests enabled for every build type so CI can run release unit tests beside the debug Compose UI suite.

nodes.name: gradlew.bat
nodes.summary: Standard Apache-licensed Gradle wrapper launcher for Windows, generated by Gradle, that locates a Java executable from JAVA_HOME or the PATH and then runs gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar with the caller's arguments. It lets Windows developers build without a local Gradle install.
nodes.languageNotes: Batch labels act as subroutines through goto and call; the line 'endlocal & "%JAVA_EXE%" ...' works because variables expand when the line is parsed, so the local scope is cleared before Java starts.

nodes.name: findJavaFromJavaHome
nodes.summary: Batch label reached when JAVA_HOME is defined: it strips quotes from JAVA_HOME, builds the bin/java.exe path, and jumps to execute when that file exists, otherwise it prints an invalid-directory error and exits with code 1.

nodes.name: execute
nodes.summary: Batch label that launches the Gradle wrapper JAR with the default JVM options plus JAVA_OPTS and GRADLE_OPTS, sets org.gradle.appname, forwards all script arguments, and then calls exitWithErrorLevel to hand back Gradle's result.

nodes.name: exitWithErrorLevel
nodes.summary: Batch subroutine that ends the script through a COMSPEC /c exit call with the current ERRORLEVEL, so callers and chained shell operators see the real Gradle exit code.

nodes.name: settings.gradle
nodes.summary: Gradle settings that centralize dependency repositories (Google, Maven Central, Sonatype snapshots, JitPack) and forbid module-level repository declarations, include the single :app module, and name the root project treetracker-android.
nodes.languageNotes: RepositoriesMode.FAIL_ON_PROJECT_REPOS makes the build fail if any module declares its own repositories, so all dependency sources stay in one place.

nodes.name: build.gradle
nodes.summary: Gradle build script for the Android app module: it sets SDK levels and version code, injects per-variant BuildConfig fields (API gateway, object storage buckets, feature flags), and defines the release, prerelease, debug, beta and dev build types. It also isolates Roborazzi screenshot tests from regular unit tests, syncs golden images with src/test/snapshots, and declares all library dependencies through the version catalog.
nodes.languageNotes: Groovy Gradle DSL. Each build type overrides the same buildConfigField keys, so Kotlin code reads one constant (for example BuildConfig.API_GATEWAY) and gets the environment chosen at build time. The dev build type adds src/debug sources through sourceSets so debug-only AppFunctions also compile there.

nodes.name: loadExtraProperties
nodes.summary: Groovy helper that reads a Java properties file and copies every key and value into the Gradle project's extra properties. The build calls it on treetracker.keys.properties at configuration time, so the buildConfigField lines can reference per-environment pool ids and client values as plain property names.

nodes.name: fab.properties
nodes.summary: Legacy Fabric tool properties file from 2018 that holds a single apiSecret entry for the old Fabric crash reporting service. No current build script reads it, because the app now uses Firebase Crashlytics and Fabric shut down in 2020.

nodes.name: fabric.properties
nodes.summary: Older copy of the Fabric crash reporting properties, generated in January 2018 with the same apiSecret key as fab.properties. It is a leftover from the pre-Firebase Crashlytics setup and has no reference in the current Gradle build.

nodes.name: google-services.json
nodes.summary: Firebase project descriptor that the google-services Gradle plugin turns into app resources, so Firebase Analytics, Crashlytics and Remote Config can start. It registers seven Android clients, one for each package name the app ships under (release, prerelease, debug, dev and test suffixes), plus a legacy package and a partner-branded variant.
nodes.languageNotes: The client entries must cover every applicationIdSuffix in app/build.gradle; the google-services plugin fails the build for a variant whose package name has no matching client.

nodes.name: 1.json
nodes.summary: Room export of AppDatabase version 1 with four tables: planter_info for grower profiles, planter_check_in for the check-in photo and GPS fix, tree_capture for each tree photo with location and accuracy, and tree_attribute for key/value capture details, linked by cascading-update foreign keys. The migration test states that exports 1 to 4 do not match the databases that shipped, so this file is history only.
nodes.languageNotes: Room writes `${TABLE_NAME}` as a placeholder in each createSql string and stores the identity hash in room_master_table through the setupQueries, so it can detect a schema mismatch at open time.

nodes.name: 2.json
nodes.summary: AppDatabase version 2 export that repeats the version 1 table layout and identity hash exactly; only the export format is newer (CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS, an empty views list, a single-quoted hash in the setup query). The migration test skips it because it does not describe a shipped database.
nodes.languageNotes: An unchanged identityHash between two versions means Room saw no entity change; the version number was raised without a structural difference.

nodes.name: 3.json
nodes.summary: AppDatabase version 3 export that adds a location_data table (uploaded flag, created_at, and a base64_json payload column, indexed on uploaded) beside the four planter and tree capture tables. Real version 3 databases still held the older legacy tables that MIGRATION_3_4 converts, so the manual migration test builds schema 3 by hand instead of from this file.

nodes.name: 4.json
nodes.summary: AppDatabase version 4 export whose only change from version 3 is a non-null record_uuid column with an empty-string default on planter_info. In the shipped upgrade path that column arrives later through MIGRATION_4_5, which is one reason the migration test treats exports 1 to 4 as inaccurate.

nodes.name: 6.json
nodes.summary: AppDatabase version 6 export, the schema of the 1.4.0 release and the oldest export that matches shipped databases (no 5.json exists). Compared with version 4 it renames the planter_info identifier column to planter_identifier, indexes planter_info on identifier and uploaded and tree_capture on uploaded, and stores location_data payloads in json_value instead of base64_json.

nodes.name: 7.json
nodes.summary: AppDatabase version 7 export that adds one index, index_planter_check_in_local_photo_path, on planter_check_in.local_photo_path, which is exactly what hand-written MIGRATION_6_7 creates. It is the last schema with only the legacy capture tables, and Room reads it at build time as the source side of the 7 to 8 AutoMigration.

nodes.name: 8.json
nodes.summary: AppDatabase version 8 export for the 2.0.0 release that adds the v2 data model next to the five legacy tables: user (wallet, photo, power_user flag), session (origin and destination wallets, start and end times, device_config link), tree (photo, note, extra_attributes, session link), location (JSON location fix per session) and device_config (app, OS and SDK versions). Room generates both the 7 to 8 and the 8 to 9 AutoMigrations from this file.
nodes.languageNotes: Room AutoMigration compares exported schema JSON at compile time, so the older exports such as 7.json and 8.json must stay in the repository. This export also lists each _id column last and adds an empty orders array to every index, a sign of a newer Room version.

nodes.name: 9.json
nodes.summary: AppDatabase version 9 export, the current schema that Room regenerates on every build and that first shipped in 2.2.0. It adds a nullable note column to session and a new organization table keyed by a text _id, with version, name, wallet_id and JSON definitions of the capture setup flow and the capture flow.

nodes.name: account.xml
nodes.summary: White 24dp Material-style person silhouette showing a head above rounded shoulders. SettingsScreen uses it as the icon of the Profile row that opens the grower profile.

nodes.name: active_arrow.xml
nodes.summary: Wide 53x15dp right-pointing arrow with a long shaft, drawn in brand green (#75B926). WalletItem in WalletSelectScreen shows it beside the selected wallet, and swaps in the gray inactive_arrow for other rows.

nodes.name: active_offer.xml
nodes.summary: 500dp illustration of an open green hand held out under a large gold coin that has a ridged edge and a two-leaf sprout on its face. WalletSelectScreen draws it as the image of every WalletItem row, at 40% alpha when the row is not selected.
nodes.languageNotes: A <group> with a <clip-path> keeps the six horizontal ridge strokes inside the coin-edge shape, a vector-drawable way to mask child paths.

nodes.name: add.xml
nodes.summary: Plus sign made of two thick, round-capped dark strokes (stroke width 7) on a 49x50dp canvas. CaptureButtons.kt draws it inside OrangeAddButton, the circular orange add button.

nodes.name: announcement_icon.xml
nodes.summary: Dark 54x44dp envelope outline with a V-shaped flap line. It is the image on the dashboard Messages button and the icon of announcement entries in IndividualMessageListScreen.

nodes.name: arrow_backward.xml
nodes.summary: Black 24dp Material back arrow that points left. arrowPainter in NavigationButtons.kt returns it when isLeft is true, so the back navigation button shows it.

nodes.name: arrow_forward.xml
nodes.summary: Black 24dp Material forward arrow that points right, the mirror image of arrow_backward. arrowPainter in NavigationButtons.kt returns it for the forward (right-side) navigation button.

nodes.name: chat_icon.xml
nodes.summary: 500dp light-gray (#d8d8d8) drawing of two person avatars that face each other, each with a speech bubble that holds two text lines. ChatScreen places it in the center of the top action bar of a direct-message conversation.

nodes.name: check.xml
