nodes.summary: Black 24dp Material checkmark glyph. ApprovalButton in ActionButtons.kt shows it on the green approve variant (approval = true) that growers tap to accept a capture.

nodes.name: close.xml
nodes.summary: White 24dp Material close glyph shaped like an X. ApprovalButton in ActionButtons.kt shows it on the red decline variant when approval is false.

nodes.name: delete.xml
nodes.summary: Red (#EA2525) 25dp trash-can icon with a separate lid bar. SettingsScreen uses it on the Delete Account row, which appears only when the DEBUG_ENABLED feature flag is on.

nodes.name: error_outline.xml
nodes.summary: Material error-outline glyph, an exclamation mark inside a ring, tinted red (#CD0C0C). It is the dialog icon of the poor-GPS warning in TreeCaptureScreen and of NoGPSDeviceDialog in GpsDialog.kt.
nodes.languageNotes: The red color comes from android:tint on the <vector> element, which recolors the white fillColor of the path at render time.

nodes.name: greenstand_logo.xml
nodes.summary: Greenstand brand mark in leaf green (#86C240): two upright leaf blades with a round dot above them, on a 1235x1549 viewport. The app reuses it as the top bar title image, the default CustomDialog icon, the privacy policy dialog header, and the small icon of the sync notification.
nodes.languageNotes: The width of 500dp and height of 627.1255dp keep the 1235:1549 viewport ratio, so the logo scales without distortion.

nodes.name: inactive_arrow.xml
nodes.summary: Gray (#585B5D) 53x16dp long right arrow, the unselected counterpart of active_arrow. WalletSelectScreen shows it beside each wallet row that the grower has not selected.

nodes.name: individual_message_icon.xml
nodes.summary: 300dp pink and magenta illustration of a person bust next to a white speech bubble with two text lines. IndividualMessageListScreen uses it for direct-message entries, and IndividualMessageItemUiTest passes it to the item under test.

nodes.name: info_icon.xml
nodes.summary: Black 24dp information glyph that shows only the letter i (a dot over a bar) without the usual surrounding circle. InfoButton in ActionButtons.kt draws it inside a round white button, for example in the tree capture top bar.

nodes.name: logout.xml
nodes.summary: White 25dp logout icon: a rounded door panel with an arrow that exits to the right, drawn with an evenOdd fill. SettingsScreen shows it on the Logout row, which is visible only when FeatureFlags.DEBUG_ENABLED is set.

nodes.name: map_icon.xml
nodes.summary: White 24dp Material folded-map glyph with three vertical panels. SettingsScreen shows it on the Map row, which appears only when the DEBUG_ENABLED or BETA feature flag is set.

nodes.name: note.xml
nodes.summary: Dark green (#507924) 17dp edit icon of a pencil over an open square. It is the dialog icon of NoteDialog on the tree image review screen and, tinted white, the icon of the Edit Trees row in SettingsScreen.

nodes.name: notification_icon.xml
nodes.summary: Black 54x48dp envelope with a filled dot at its top-right corner that signals unread content. It is the unread badge on dashboard buttons, on IndividualMessageListItem rows, and on SelectableItemDetail items.

nodes.name: open_mailbox_with_lowered_flag.xml
nodes.summary: Colorful 242x200dp illustration of an open blue mailbox on a brown post with its red flag lowered, which means nothing waits inside. NoMessages.kt shows it for an empty message list, and TreeListScreen reuses it when there are no trees to edit.

nodes.name: privacy_policy.xml
nodes.summary: White 24dp outline icon of a document with text lines and a folded corner, plus a small shield at the lower right. SettingsScreen uses it on the Privacy row that opens the privacy policy dialog.
nodes.languageNotes: Both paths use a transparent fillColor with 1.5-unit round strokes, so the icon is pure line art and keeps a constant line weight.

nodes.name: quiz_icon.xml
nodes.summary: 300dp illustration of an orange question mark with branching arrows that lead to three answer circles marked A, B and C, over a translucent magenta shadow layer. IndividualMessageListScreen uses it for survey messages.

nodes.name: selfie_illustration.xml
nodes.summary: 131x157dp illustration of a person with dark curly hair in a green top who holds a phone up for a selfie, with the preview on the phone screen and white sparkles nearby. SelfieTutorial in Tutorial.kt shows it with the selfie instructions, and TutorialUiTest renders it.

nodes.name: settings_filled.xml
nodes.summary: Green (#75B926) 50dp filled icon of two cog wheels, one large and one small. DashboardTopBar draws it as the clickable settings button at the left of the dashboard action bar.

nodes.name: touch_gesture.xml
nodes.summary: White 49dp Material touch-app glyph: a pointing hand with a tap ring around the fingertip. The capture review tutorial in Tutorial.kt places it under the Note, approve and decline buttons to show the grower where to tap.

nodes.name: track_icon.xml
nodes.summary: 500dp icon of a young sapling with three outlined green leaves that grows out of a gray planting pot, drawn with thick dark strokes (width 11.25). The dashboard Track button in DashboardActions shows it, and DashboardComponentsUiTest uses it.

nodes.name: tree_capturing_illustration.xml
nodes.summary: 169x160dp scene of a grower in green clothing who points a phone at a small three-leaf seedling on a brown ground line. It illustrates TreeCaptureTutorial and is the placeholder image in TreeListScreen and TreeDetailScreen when a tree has no photo.

nodes.name: upload_icon.xml
nodes.summary: Dark 42x66dp phone outline with an upward arrow on its screen that stands for upload. It is the image on the dashboard Upload button and the small icon of the ongoing TreeSyncWorker notification.

nodes.name: colors.xml
nodes.summary: Defines the app's XML color palette: the dark green brand primary and accent (#1B5E20), black, white and red, a newer light green palette, and component aliases such as toolbar, button and background that point at palette entries instead of hex values. Kotlin uses only colorPrimary, to tint sync notifications, and the XML theme reads the primary, dark and accent colors.

nodes.name: dimens.xml
nodes.summary: Lists 51 dp and sp dimension values for screen margins, paddings, heights, logo size, button borders and text sizes, left over from the older XML layout UI. No Kotlin or XML file in the current source refers to these dimensions, because the Compose screens set their sizes in code.
nodes.languageNotes: Several names do not match their values (for example text_size_sixty is 16sp), which is a sign that the values were edited after the names were chosen.

nodes.name: font_certs.xml
nodes.summary: Holds the Google Play Services font provider certificate arrays (one development and one production signing certificate, Base64 encoded) that Android needs to verify downloadable Google Fonts. The app bundles its Montserrat fonts as local .ttf files, so no font request in the current source uses these certificates.
nodes.languageNotes: This is the standard file that Android Studio generates for downloadable fonts; a typed array wraps the two string-arrays so a font request can accept either certificate.

nodes.name: ic_launcher_background.xml
nodes.summary: Declares the single white color resource ic_launcher_background. Both adaptive launcher icon definitions in mipmap-anydpi-v26 use it as the background layer behind the foreground artwork.

nodes.name: ids.xml
nodes.summary: Reserves one static view ID, splash_fragment, in the R.id namespace. Nothing in the current source refers to it, so it appears to be a leftover from an earlier fragment-based splash screen.

nodes.name: preloaded_fonts.xml
nodes.summary: Defines the non-translatable preloaded_fonts array, which contains only the bundled Montserrat Bold font. The main manifest points its preloaded_fonts meta-data at this array so Android loads the font early, and the Compose theme uses the same font for bold text.

nodes.name: strings.xml
nodes.summary: Default English string table with 152 user-facing texts: sync status messages, login and sign-up hints, permission rationales, weak GPS help, tutorial prompts, settings and profile labels, tree list and tree detail labels, name validation errors, and the full privacy policy that the privacy dialog shows. Compose screens and view models read these entries through R.string, the values-pt and values-sw files translate them, and build.gradle injects app_name separately for each build type.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Android string resource escapes (\' for apostrophes, \n for line breaks), inline <b> markup for bold text, and positional format arguments such as %1$s and %2$d. The file starts with a UTF-8 byte order mark.

nodes.name: styles.xml
nodes.summary: Defines the XML theme AppTheme, which extends Theme.AppCompat.Light.NoActionBar with the brand primary, primary dark and accent colors, and its child AppTheme.NoActionBar, which turns off the window action bar and title. The main manifest applies AppTheme to the application and AppTheme.NoActionBar to its activities, and the debug manifest uses AppTheme.NoActionBar for the E2E test activity.

nodes.name: architecture.md
nodes.summary: Engineering guide to the app's MVVM design: BaseViewModel with a typed Action sealed class, the stateful Root versus stateless UI composable split, and previews plus Roborazzi snapshot tests that target the stateless layer. It also names the three Koin modules (AppModule, RoomModule, NetworkModule) and the core stack of Compose, Retrofit, Room, AWS S3, CameraX, coroutines, and Firebase.
nodes.languageNotes: The Kotlin snippets dispatch a sealed Action class with an exhaustive `when`, so the compiler flags any unhandled UI action. One early example resolves the ViewModel with koinViewModel(), while the later Root example uses LocalViewModelFactory, which is the form the screen code actually uses.

nodes.name: data-entities.md
nodes.summary: Reference for the legacy Room entities that store planter identity, check-ins, tree captures, per-capture key-value attributes, and streamed location data, with the key columns of each table (planter_info, planter_check_in, tree_capture, tree_attribute, location_data). It embeds an ER diagram and points to the sync page for upload orchestration.

nodes.name: data-sync-architecture.md
nodes.summary: Describes the six-step background sync that TreeSyncWorker runs through SyncDataUseCase: messages, device config, planters, sessions, legacy and new trees, then location data. It also gives the shared uploader recipe of S3 image upload, JSON bundle upload through ObjectStorageClient, mark-as-uploaded, and local image cleanup.

nodes.name: kotlin-migration.md
nodes.summary: Short historical note that records the project's completed move to Kotlin and keeps one link to the official Kotlin tutorials for developers who are new to the language.

nodes.name: navigation-flows.md
nodes.summary: Maps the app's multi-step navigation: the signup flow (privacy policy, phone or email, name, selfie), the capture setup flow run by CaptureSetupNavigationController, the looping capture flow run by CaptureFlowNavigationController with optional height and DBH steps, and the messaging flow. It also lists standalone screens such as Splash, Language Select, Organization Select, and Dashboard.

nodes.name: package-structure.md
nodes.summary: Lists the top-level packages under org.greenstand.android.TreeTracker and the job of each one, from activities, api, and background workers to database, di, messages, navigation, usecases, and the reusable Compose components in view.

nodes.name: preferences-and-prefkeys.md
nodes.summary: Explains how the Preferences wrapper over SharedPreferences uses typed PrefKey objects that compose into path-like namespaces, and how UserPrefKey scopes a key to the current user on shared devices. It shows that keys under PrefKeys.SESSION are cleared on logout, while ROOT and SYSTEM_SETTINGS keys persist.

nodes.name: upload-business-logic.md
nodes.summary: Walks through the upload sequence that SyncDataUseCase drives from TreeSyncWorker, and the common steps that TreeUploader, PlanterUploader, and SessionUploader share, from reading Room rows to deleting uploaded photos. Its content closely duplicates the Data Sync Architecture page.

nodes.name: user-login-logic.md
nodes.summary: Work-in-progress design notes on shared-device login, where repeated identifier-plus-photo check-ins attribute tree captures to the right planter for payout verification, also offline and for low-literacy users. It separates one-per-device planter profile records from many time-bounded check-in records.

nodes.name: build-variants.md
nodes.summary: Lists the five Gradle build variants (dev, debug, beta, prerelease, release) and what sets each apart: relaxed accuracy for dev, blur detection in debug, the test environment for beta, and production endpoints with minification for release.

nodes.name: common-commands.md
nodes.summary: Cheat sheet of Gradle wrapper commands that assemble each variant, run unit and instrumented tests, and run the ktlint, detekt, and spotless code-quality tasks, plus the Bundler and Fastlane setup steps for deployment.

nodes.name: environment-setup.md
nodes.summary: Developer setup guide that names the required Android Studio and JDK 25 tooling and SDK levels (compile 37, target 36, min 23), suggests a GPS faker for indoor device tests, and gives five steps from placing treetracker.keys.properties to running the dev variant.

nodes.name: prerequisites.md
nodes.summary: States the two hard requirements before a build: the treetracker.keys.properties file with storage credentials and API client settings, requested from the Android team chat, and a JDK 25 install that JAVA_HOME must point to when Gradle runs from a terminal.

nodes.name: project-overview.md
nodes.summary: Brief introduction that frames Treetracker Android as a field app which captures tree growth data and uploads verifiable records to Greenstand services, in support of climate restoration and income for tree growers. It links to the product documentation and the architecture page.

nodes.name: add-tree-flow.md
nodes.summary: Describes the Add Tree flow that planters start from the dashboard. One flow serves both new tree captures and growth updates of existing trees, and the server decides which is which. It also explains the GPS convergence gate: a progress indicator runs until recent location samples converge, or until a timeout lets capture go ahead anyway.

nodes.name: device-data-capture.md
nodes.summary: Lists the device telemetry that the app records for captures (GPS, step count, gyroscope and compass heading). It explains how this data supports location convergence, the split between updates and new trees, and image interpretation during verification, and it links to a legacy wiki page on v1.4 GPS data collection.

nodes.name: next-gen-advanced-app.md
nodes.summary: Backlog of exploratory feature ideas from legacy wiki notes: login and account deduplication, better org selection, reusable species input, multiple FMNR before/after images, an explicit photo retake, a richer map tree detail view, and an image review/delete flow. It states that the list is not a committed implementation plan.

nodes.name: org-link-features.md
nodes.summary: Specification of the org link deep link (app://mobile.treetracker.org/org?id=&name=) and of the Firebase Remote Config JSON under key org_config_{id}. The JSON sets the destination wallet, the ordered setup-flow and capture-flow routes, and per-route feature flags such as forceNote. The page also covers route aliases, silent removal of unknown routes, the 10-second offline fallback to default flows, and adb commands for four test orgs.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Markdown tables to map route strings and aliases to screens, and fenced JSON blocks as copy-ready Remote Config payloads.

nodes.name: org-links.md
nodes.summary: Design note on org links: deep links that add or update an organization's theme, features and flow settings on the device, so that the project needs fewer per-org app flavors and no manual org entry. It also describes the debug-only Org Link Overrides in Dev Options, which let testers switch steps, features and the wallet ID without a new link.

nodes.name: product-documentation.md
nodes.summary: Top-level product overview of the Treetracker mobile app. It covers the climate and livelihood goals, the three user groups (organizational trackers, village coordinators, individual growers), offline and low-battery field constraints, identity and check-in concepts, and the verification and payout context, and it links to the detailed product pages.

nodes.name: roadmap.md
nodes.summary: Short roadmap index that points to the Org Links design note and to the Next-Gen Advanced App ideas list as the current and legacy roadmap references.

nodes.name: user-stories.md
nodes.summary: Records the functional criteria for the app (offline use, battery life, simplicity, GPS reliance, verifiable data) and the field challenges such as sunlight glare, poor connectivity, low literacy and shared devices. It also gives three core capture user stories and names the primary and secondary target users.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Task record for issue #1401, which added end-to-end flows for developer tools: dev options parameter persistence (I1) and debug overlay toggles during capture and sync (I2). It describes the device seeding script, the debug-only E2eActivity deep links, the run script and the CI job on API 35, the validation results, and known limits such as the API 37 camera crash and a slow Test Buddy runner.

nodes.name: api37-camera-bug.md
nodes.summary: Draft bug report for a crash on an API 37 emulator: CameraX 1.4.1 throws a NullPointerException in bindToLifecycle because it cannot map dynamic range profile 8192, so the capture screen fails before the shutter is usable. It records the environment, the stack trace through Camera.kt, and the decision to keep the E2E suite on API 35.

nodes.name: e2e-dev-tools.xml
nodes.summary: JUnit XML report from the recorded Test Buddy run of the dev-tools tagged flows on an arm64 emulator. Both the I2 debug overlays flow (150.8 s) and the I1 dev options flow (19.7 s) passed, and the task 49 record links this file as evidence.

nodes.name: e2e-first-screen.xml
nodes.summary: JUnit XML report that shows the first-screen E2E flow passed in 3.75 seconds on an arm64 emulator, run before device seeding. The task 49 record links it as validation evidence for first launch.

nodes.name: agent-app-functions.md
nodes.summary: Guide to the debug-only Android AppFunctions `createAccount` and `captureTrees`, which let an agent seed accounts and trees over adb instead of driving the sign-up and capture screens. It gives the API 37 requirement, the adb quoting rules, the parameter tables and defaults, gotchas such as lost permissions after `pm clear`, a clean-install recipe, and where the Kotlin and shell code lives.
nodes.languageNotes: The device shell parses `adb shell` arguments a second time, so the JSON parameters are wrapped in escaped single quotes to keep their double quotes intact.

nodes.name: app-distribution-testing.md
nodes.summary: Manual QA checklist for beta builds that testers install from a Firebase App Distribution invitation. It lists seven core checks (phone or email login, re-login, user switching, GPS-gated tree capture, image upload, sync, data visible in the admin tools), what each test report records, and where to file defects.

nodes.name: ci-flows.md
nodes.summary: Operator guide for the Flow runner, which runs Test Buddy flows on the CI emulator for any branch or PR and brings back per-step screenshots, logs, logcat and videos to a cloud session that has no emulator. It covers flow selectors, the label, comment and script triggers, the affected-flows job that traces a diff to flows through TestTags ids, before and after validating flows with their verdicts, the results layout, lost-recording retries and fork PR handling.

nodes.name: e2e-flow-test-plan.md
nodes.summary: Audit and roadmap for a black-box Test Buddy flow suite that should catch broken contributor PRs and prove nothing regresses during the KMP/CMP move. It maps the 29 Navigation 3 routes, inventories the existing tests, proposes prioritized flows (signup, capture, org-configured variants, sync, settings, messages, org links, sad paths, dev tools) with their coverage, and records code findings such as process-death scope crashes and back-stack bugs with their fix issues.

nodes.name: testing.md
nodes.summary: Top-level testing guide for the app: JVM unit tests with MockK, Turbine and a coroutine rule, Robolectric Compose UI tests on the ComposeUiTest base class, Test Buddy end-to-end flows run by `e2e/run.sh` and CI, and Roborazzi screenshot tests. It also explains the Robolectric setup that keeps the Application class and Koin out of tests, and links the other QA docs.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Guide to the Test Buddy (tb) end-to-end suite: it lists each flow family with its tag (signup, capture, settings, sad-path, org-config, dev-tools, known-bug) and its test-plan ids, and explains how to run the flows on a disposable emulator. It also documents the debug-only treetracker-e2e:// seed links, the TestTags resource ids that flows tap, and the screen tour script.

nodes.name: run.sh
nodes.summary: Entry point for the whole end-to-end suite on one named disposable emulator, used locally and by the Android end-to-end CI check. It switches the device offline, runs every flow except the dev-tools, org-config and known-bug ones, runs the org-config flows through run-org.sh, then seeds fixtures with setup-device.sh and runs the dev-tools flows, writing JUnit reports under build/e2e.
nodes.languageNotes: A `trap cleanup EXIT` handler restores the network state captured at start even when `set -e` aborts the script after a failed tb run.

nodes.name: cleanup
nodes.summary: EXIT trap handler that force-stops the debug app to cancel outstanding sync work, then puts the emulator's airplane mode and Wi-Fi back to the values recorded before the run.

nodes.name: run-org.sh
nodes.summary: Runs the six org-config flows one at a time, re-seeding the emulator with the matching org variant through seed-org.sh before each flow, because every flow needs its own capture configuration in the database. A failed seed or flow is noted and the loop continues, so the exit status reports any failure at the end.
nodes.languageNotes: The variant-to-flow table is a heredoc read with `while read`; each child gets `</dev/null` so it cannot consume the loop's stdin. run-flows.sh parses the same table with awk.

nodes.name: seed-org.sh
nodes.summary: Prepares an org-configured scenario on a debug emulator: it resets the app and seeds Ada Admin through setup-device.sh, then inserts an organization row whose capture setup and capture flow JSON match the session-note, tree-height, force-note or wallet-select variant, and marks it as the current org. This replaces Firebase Remote Config, which an offline emulator cannot reach.
nodes.languageNotes: The SQL goes to a temp file that is pushed to the device and fed to sqlite3 through `adb shell run-as`; the current-org preference is added with a sed insertion before `</map>` in the app's shared_prefs XML.

nodes.name: setup-device.sh
nodes.summary: Wipes and seeds one named debug emulator with Ada Admin and two trees, then deep-links to the dashboard, dev-options or capture screen. On API 37+ it calls the agent AppFunctions through app_fn.sh (reset, createAccount, captureTrees); on API 35/36 it opens the treetracker-e2e://setup link and polls a result file until the same seeding helpers report ready.

nodes.name: affected-overrides.json
nodes.summary: Hint table for affected.py's choice of flows a PR affects. For screens built from shared components (user cards, the capture button, review buttons) it lists the test-tag ids that show a flow is on the screen and the ids or sub-flow after which that holds, plus an ignore list of path globs.

nodes.name: cloud-flows.sh
nodes.summary: Command-line bridge that lets a session without an emulator, such as a Claude Code cloud session, run Test Buddy flows on CI. Its run, pr, wait and fetch subcommands dispatch the flow-runner workflow or label a PR with run-flows, poll the Actions run through gh, and download screenshots, logs and verdicts from the flow-results branch.
nodes.languageNotes: Subcommands are a top-level `case` on $1; `gh api --jq` does the JSON filtering, and an inline Python program rewrites the PR description's run-flows line with a multiline regex.

nodes.name: pr_for_branch
nodes.summary: Looks up the number of the open pull request whose head is the given branch through the GitHub REST API, and prints nothing when no such PR exists.

nodes.name: wait_run
nodes.summary: Polls one GitHub Actions run every POLL seconds for up to 90 minutes, printing each status change and riding out transient Not Found or API errors, and returns once the run has completed whatever its conclusion.

nodes.name: fetch
nodes.summary: Shallow-fetches a flow-results branch into a local ref, extracts it into the output folder with git archive, warns when the stored runId is not the expected run, and prints the verdict and summary markdown.

nodes.name: cmd_run
nodes.summary: Implements the run subcommand: it parses selectors and options (ref, PR, inline flow, video, API level, screenshots, validate with a before commit), checks that the branch is pushed, dispatches flow-runner.yml with matching inputs, finds the new run id, then waits and fetches the results unless --no-wait is given.

nodes.name: results_branch
nodes.summary: Names the git branch where CI stores a run's results: flow-results/pr-N when a PR number is known, otherwise flow-results/run-ID.

nodes.name: cmd_pr
nodes.summary: Implements the pr subcommand: it optionally writes the selectors onto a run-flows line in the PR description, adds or re-adds the run-flows label to start flow-runner-pr.yml, finds the runs created for the PR head commit since then, waits for all of them and fetches the PR's results branch.

nodes.name: run-flows.sh
nodes.summary: Core flow runner used by the flow-runner CI job and locally: it resolves selectors (path, name, glob, tag:, name@N step cuts) to flow files and runs each Test Buddy flow on its own on an offline emulator, with org or dev-tools seeding, per-step screenshots and optional video with retries for lost recordings. It then gathers logcat, crash logs and artifacts per flow, writes results.tsv and a summary, and exits 0, 1, 2 or 3 for passed, failed, bad input or lost recording.
nodes.languageNotes: Plain indexed arrays (FLOWS, CUTS) replace associative arrays so the script still runs on macOS bash 3.2, and FLOW_SELECTORS is split under `set -f` so globs in it are not expanded.

nodes.name: has_tag
nodes.summary: Asks flowfile.py whether a flow file carries a given tag, so tag selectors use the same YAML tag parsing as affected.py, including inline and block lists with comments.

nodes.name: add
nodes.summary: Appends resolved flow files to the run list without repeats while merging step cuts: a whole-flow request overrides a cut, and of two cuts the longer one wins.

nodes.name: warm_up_pulls
nodes.summary: Absorbs the CI emulator's early adb pull drops before any recording matters, by pulling a 1 MB scratch file until five pulls succeed in a row (at most 20 tries), then reports how many dropped.

nodes.name: start_recording
nodes.summary: Starts a background adb shell loop that records the screen in 170-second screenrecord parts under /sdcard/flow-rec until a stop marker file appears, and keeps the loop's process id.

nodes.name: pull_video
nodes.summary: Copies one video file off the device with up to three adb pull attempts, waiting for the device to reconnect between tries, since the file stays on the emulator after a dropped connection.

nodes.name: stop_recording
nodes.summary: Ends screen recording for a flow: it touches the stop marker, interrupts screenrecord and waits for it to exit, pulls each part, then renames a single part or joins several with ffmpeg into videos/<flow>.mp4.

nodes.name: run_once
nodes.summary: Runs one flow a single time: it force-stops the app, seeds the org variant listed in run-org.sh or the dev-tools fixtures, builds a step-cut and screenshot-instrumented copy of the flow with cut_flow.py and step_shots.py, runs tb with JUnit output and optional annotated recording, and records STATUS, elapsed time and logcat.

nodes.name: record_trouble
nodes.summary: Extracts tb's first '--record:' complaint from the flow's console log, trimmed to 300 characters, to explain why a recording was lost or only partly saved.

nodes.name: tb_recorded
nodes.summary: Succeeds when tb's debug output for the flow holds a non-empty recording*.mp4; the retry loop uses it to decide whether an annotated flow must run again.

nodes.name: run-job.sh
nodes.summary: Job script that flow-runner-job.yml runs on the emulator: it runs the chosen flows through run-flows.sh, then for validating flows installs the base branch app and the PR app in turn, runs those flows on each with annotated video, and gets a before-and-after verdict from verdict.py. Last, it converts every MP4 into a small GIF that a PR comment can play inline.

nodes.name: note
nodes.summary: Folds one run-flows.sh exit status into the job's state: status 3 marks a lost recording, and any other non-zero status marks a failure.

nodes.name: install
nodes.summary: Uninstalls the debug app and then installs the given APK, so the base and PR builds never share a database version on the emulator.

nodes.name: capture-exit-profile-next.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro flow B5b that signs up an admin, starts capture, then taps the profile icon to end the session and land on user select. It checks that picking the same user and tapping Next opens Add org and goes on into capture, which guards against the 'CaptureSetupScope not open' crash.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a conditional runFlow with a 'when: visible' clause, so the capture tutorial is dismissed only if it appears.

nodes.name: capture-exit.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro flow B5 that enters capture three times and leaves it by a different route each time. System back and the on-screen back arrow must both return to the Dashboard, while the profile icon must open user select with neither Track nor Capture visible.

nodes.name: capture-first-tree.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro flow B1 for the core happy path: a new admin signs up, starts capture, takes one photo, dismisses the capture tutorial and approves the image. Back on the Dashboard it asserts that the trees-to-sync counter reads 1.

nodes.name: capture-loop.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro flow B2 that captures and approves a first tree, then repeats the capture and approve cycle twice more without leaving the capture screen. It verifies that the Dashboard counter of trees to sync reaches 3, which proves that the capture loop saves every tree.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the Maestro 'repeat' command with 'times: 2' to run the same capture and approve block in a loop.

nodes.name: capture-new-user.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro flow B6 that adds a second grower in the middle of capture setup: from user select it taps the add button, closes the privacy policy, enters a phone number and a name, and takes a selfie. It checks that setup then goes on to Add org instead of the Dashboard and reaches the capture screen.

nodes.name: capture-note.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro flow B4 that attaches the note 'Oak by the gate' through the note dialog on the image review screen before it approves the tree. It then opens Settings, Edit trees, the user and the first tree, and asserts that the tree detail note field shows the saved text.

nodes.name: capture-reject.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro flow B3 that takes a photo and taps Decline on the image review screen, then goes back through capture to the Dashboard. It asserts that the trees-to-sync counter stays at 0, so a rejected photo is not saved as a tree.

nodes.name: debug-overlays.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro flow I2 that opens hidden dev options through the treetracker-e2e deep link, turns on the sync and sensor diagnostic overlays, and toggles them from the floating debug menu on capture and on the Dashboard. It starts a real offline upload and waits for the sync overlay error to prove that the worker tried to sync, takes screenshots, and leaves both overlays off.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses 'openLink' with a custom treetracker-e2e:// scheme to jump to seeded screens, and 'takeScreenshot' to keep visual evidence of the overlay states.

nodes.name: dev-options.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro flow I1 that opens dev options with a long press on the top bar logo and toggles the 'Force Image Size' developer parameter. It checks that the switch state survives back navigation and a full stop and relaunch of the app, and that the restored default is saved too.

nodes.name: first-screen.yaml
nodes.summary: Minimal smoke flow that launches a fresh install with cleared state and waits up to 30 seconds for the language picker to show 'ENGLISH'. It confirms that the splash screen goes straight on to language selection when the runtime permissions are granted at launch.
nodes.languageNotes: A Maestro flow is two YAML documents: a header (appId, name, tags) and, after the '---' separator, the command list.

nodes.name: org-double-tap-session-note.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro flow H8 for an org seeded with a session note step: it double taps Next on user select and asserts that the second tap is dropped, so the session note screen stays open and capture does not start. A single Next tap afterwards must still reach capture, which covers the DoubleTapGuard fix.

nodes.name: org-force-note.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro flow C3 for an org seeded with the forceNote capture feature: approving a photo without a note must open the note dialog and keep the review screen. After it enters 'Planted beside the river' the approval succeeds, the loop returns to capture, and the Dashboard shows 3 trees to sync.

nodes.name: org-process-death-session-note.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro flow C5 that sends the app to the background on the org session note setup step, kills its process, and reopens it from recents. It checks that the session note screen comes back without a crash and that Next still finishes setup and opens capture, because the step restores the setup scope and the saved user.
nodes.languageNotes: Simulates Android process death with 'pressKey: Home' plus 'killApp', then 'launchApp: {stopApp: false}' so that the system restores the saved navigation state.

nodes.name: org-session-note.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro flow C1 for an org whose setup includes a session note step: it types 'Planting day at the school' on the session note screen, goes on into capture, and approves one tree. It verifies that the session note step leads to capture and that the Dashboard ends with 3 trees to sync.

nodes.name: org-tree-height.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro flow C2 for an org that adds a tree height step after image review: after it approves a photo, it picks the first height colour and taps Next. It checks that the capture loop then returns to the camera and that the Dashboard shows 3 trees to sync.

nodes.name: org-wallet-select.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro flow C4 that runs two capture sessions for an org with a wallet select step: the first session picks the existing grower wallet, the second adds a new wallet named 'Tree Fund'. Each session approves one tree, and the flow asserts that the Dashboard counter goes from 3 to 4.

nodes.name: returning-user-relaunch.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro flow E1-E2 for a returning user: after signup, a cold relaunch must go from the splash screen straight to the Dashboard with no language picker and no signup. It then changes the language to Swahili from the top bar, checks that Settings reads 'Mipangilio', and confirms that the choice survives another relaunch.

nodes.name: sad-back-add-org.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro regression flow H9 for issue #1422: it signs up, reaches Add org from user select, presses system back to user select, and taps Next again. It asserts that Add org opens a second time and that the app does not skip straight into capture.

nodes.name: sad-back.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro flow H9 that presses system back on 15 screens and asserts where each one lands, as listed in the from and to table in its header: image review, capture, capture setup, language picker, messages, profile, edit trees, map and Settings. It saves one tree first so that the tree list and map have data, and it ends with a check that back on the Dashboard leaves the app.
nodes.languageNotes: The header comment holds a Markdown table of expected back destinations, so the flow doubles as navigation documentation.

nodes.name: sad-camera-denied.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro flow H2 that revokes the camera permission after signup and denies it again on the splash screen, which still reaches the Dashboard because only location is required there. On capture it checks two denial paths: a cancel on the camera rationale dialog returns to Add org, and 'don't ask again' shows the dialog that points to the app settings.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses 'setPermissions' and per-launch 'permissions' to deny camera access, and taps the Android system dialog buttons by their resource ids (permission_deny_button).

nodes.name: sad-camera-rationale-next.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro sad-path flow (H2) that denies the camera permission, enters capture setup through user select and Add org, then backs out of the system camera prompt and cancels the camera rationale dialog. It checks that the app returns to Add org and that Next there opens capture again and asks for the camera, which proves the capture setup scope stays open while its screens are on the back stack (#1421).

nodes.name: sad-capture-after-process-death.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro sad-path flow (H6/H10) that saves one tree, has Android kill the app on the capture screen, and reopens it from recents to capture a second tree. It checks that the restored capture screen resumes GPS updates so the photo reaches image review without the bad GPS dialog, and that the Dashboard then counts 2 trees to sync (#1420).

nodes.name: sad-double-tap-setup.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro sad-path flow (H8) that double-taps Track on the Dashboard and Next on user select, then uses the back arrow on Add org. It checks that each double tap pushes only one screen, so back lands on user select with no capture screen behind it; DoubleTapGuard and the repeat-call guard in CaptureSetupNavigationController.navForward make this hold on small CI screens (#1423).

nodes.name: sad-double-tap.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro sad-path flow (H8) that double-taps the Settings button on the Dashboard and the Edit trees row in Settings. It checks that each double tap opens its target screen only once, so one system back returns to the Dashboard or to Settings where the tap started.

nodes.name: sad-interrupted-session.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro sad-path flow (H10) that kills the app during capture sessions and comes back in two ways: a relaunch from recents that restores the capture screen, and a cold start that runs the splash screen's SessionTracker.wasSessionInterrupted recount. It checks the Dashboard trees-to-sync count after each path (1, then 2) and that a third session after the interruption still saves a tree, ending at 3.

nodes.name: sad-location-denied.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro sad-path flow (H1) for a fresh install that allows camera and notifications, denies location in the system dialog on the splash screen, and allows physical activity when Android asks. It checks that the app still leaves the splash screen and lands on language select instead of closing or crashing (#1417).
nodes.languageNotes: launchApp sets runtime permissions before start; location left unanswered makes Android show its own dialog, which the flow answers through the system permission_deny_button id. A conditional runFlow with when: visible handles the optional physical activity prompt.

nodes.name: sad-process-death-review.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro sad-path flow (H6) that takes a photo but has Android kill the app on image review before approval, then reopens it from recents. It checks that image review comes back without a crash, that approving saves the tree exactly once, and that a second capture in the same session brings the Dashboard count to 2.

nodes.name: sad-process-death-screens.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro sad-path flow (H7) that kills the app process while the Dashboard shows and again while Settings shows, and reopens it from recents each time. It checks that the same screen comes back without a crash (the Dashboard with 0 trees to sync, then Settings) and that back from the restored Settings still reaches the Dashboard.
nodes.languageNotes: Maestro simulates process death with pressKey Home, killApp, and launchApp with stopApp: false, which reopens the app from recents so Android restores the saved instance state.

nodes.name: sad-process-death-setup.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro sad-path flow (H5) that has Android kill the app on the Add org step of capture setup and reopens it from recents. It checks that Add org comes back without a crash and that Next still finishes setup and opens the capture screen, because AddOrgViewModel reopens the setup scope and reloads the setup user saved before the kill (#1418).

nodes.name: settings-delete-admin.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro settings flow (E8) that deletes the only user, the admin, through Settings, Delete account, user select, and the confirm dialog. It checks the "Account Deleted" dialog, that closing it opens Signup behind the privacy policy, and that after a relaunch the app starts over on the language picker with no Dashboard.

nodes.name: settings-delete-user-offline.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro settings flow that signs up Ada, adds a second user Bob from user select, and deletes Bob in Settings while the device is in airplane mode. It is the regression check for #1416: the failed message sync after the delete must not crash the app, the "Account Deleted" dialog must return to Settings, and the Delete account list must keep Ada without Bob.

nodes.name: settings-delete-user.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro settings flow (E7) that adds a non-admin user Bob, opens Delete account in Settings, cancels the confirm dialog once, and then confirms. It checks that cancel keeps Bob, that confirming shows "Account Deleted" and returns to Settings, and that after a relaunch the Delete account list holds only the admin.

nodes.name: settings-logout-back.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro settings flow that logs out from Settings, then signs back in by entering the existing phone number and picking the existing-user option. It checks that system back on the Dashboard exits the app instead of returning to Signup, since Signup clears the whole back stack when it opens the Dashboard.

nodes.name: settings-logout.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro settings flow (E6) that opens the logout confirmation, cancels it once, then confirms and signs in again with the same phone number. It checks that cancel keeps the user in Settings, that confirming opens Signup with no Dashboard or Settings controls visible, and that back from the Dashboard after the new sign-in exits the app.

nodes.name: settings-profile-edit.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro settings flow (E10) that goes to Settings, Profile, picks the user, taps Edit, and replaces the first and last name with Grace Hopper before it saves. It checks that the new name shows at once and is still there after a relaunch, with the wallet unchanged, so the edit reached the database; UserRepoTest and PlanterUploaderTest cover the upload, because CI runs offline.

nodes.name: settings-profile-privacy.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro settings flow (E3, E9) for the read-only Settings paths: it opens and closes the privacy policy dialog, then views the profile of the signed-up user. It checks that the profile shows Ada, Admin, and the wallet number, and that three system backs return through profile select and Settings to the Dashboard.

nodes.name: settings-trees-map.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro settings flow (E4, E5) that captures one tree, opens the Settings Map to find its card, and then opens the tree in Edit trees to save a note and delete the tree. It checks the snackbar after the save, that the note is kept when the tree opens again, that cancel keeps the tree and confirm empties the list, and that the Map then shows no cards.

nodes.name: signup-back.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro signup flow (A6) that walks backward through signup on a fresh install. It checks that system back on the credential step returns to the language picker, that the on-screen back arrow on the name step returns to the credential step with the phone number kept, and that system back on the name step leaves signup for the language picker.

nodes.name: signup-email.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro signup flow (A2) that runs the shared signup subflow with an email address instead of a phone number on a fresh install. It checks that the new user reaches an empty Dashboard with 0 trees to sync and 0 trees synced.
nodes.languageNotes: The runFlow env block passes CREDENTIAL: Email to the shared subflow, whose conditional runFlow blocks pick the email or the phone path.

nodes.name: signup-existing-user.yaml
nodes.summary: Maestro signup flow (A5) that, after the first signup, adds a user from user select with the same phone number again. It checks that the existing-user dialog shows instead of the name step, that cancel stays on the credential step, and that picking the existing user goes on to Add org, since an admin already exists.

nodes.name: signup-phone.yaml
nodes.summary: End-to-end flow A1 that clears the debug app's state, signs up Ada Admin with phone number 5551230001 through the shared signup subflow, and asserts that the new Dashboard shows 0 trees to sync and 0 trees synced.
nodes.languageNotes: Maestro-style YAML in two documents: a header (appId, name, tags) above the `---` line and a command list below it. The `runFlow` command passes `env` values into the reusable subflow.

nodes.name: signup-selfie-retake.yaml
nodes.summary: End-to-end flow A4 that signs up by hand, declines the first selfie and retakes it before approval, then starts a second signup from the user picker and backs out of the selfie camera. It checks that the name step keeps the typed name and that the user picker lists only the first user, so a cancelled signup creates no account.
nodes.languageNotes: The flow inlines the signup steps instead of calling the signup subflow, because it must interrupt the sequence at the selfie camera. It waits with `extendedWaitUntil` for the slow camera screens and checks absence with `assertNotVisible`.

nodes.name: signup-validation.yaml
nodes.summary: End-to-end flow A3 for signup input validation: an invalid phone ("123") and an invalid email ("nope") each show a snackbar and keep the credential step, and a one-letter first name and a last name typed as "B1!" (filtered to "B") show field errors and disable Next. Fixing both names clears the errors and lets the user continue through the tutorial and the selfie to the Dashboard.
nodes.languageNotes: The flow asserts element state with `assertVisible: {id: ..., enabled: false}`, and it appends text to the current field value ("@example.com", "da", "dmin") instead of clearing the field.

nodes.name: org-capture-setup.yaml
nodes.summary: Reusable subflow for the org-config flows: on a device where seed-org.sh has written a custom org, it waits for the Dashboard Track button, picks Ada Admin's user card (wallet 5551230001), and taps Next onto the first setup step that the org defines. It has no tags, so the flow runner starts it only through `runFlow`.
nodes.languageNotes: Unlike the other subflows, it hard-codes the wallet id in `UserButton_5551230001` because the seed script always creates the same user.

nodes.name: signup.yaml
nodes.summary: Shared signup subflow that takes a fresh install from the language picker through the privacy policy, the credential step, the name step, the tutorial, and the selfie approval, and ends when the Dashboard Track button appears. The env values CREDENTIAL, IDENTIFIER, FIRST_NAME and LAST_NAME set the account, and nearly every signup, capture, settings and sad-path flow calls it to create its starting user.
nodes.languageNotes: Two conditional `runFlow` blocks with `when: {true: "${...}"}` JavaScript expressions select the email or the phone credential tab, which gives a branch without a separate file.

nodes.name: start-capture.yaml
nodes.summary: Reusable subflow that starts a capture session from the Dashboard: it taps Track, picks the user card for the WALLET env value, accepts the default org on the add-org screen, closes the capture tutorial only if it shows, and waits up to 30 seconds for the capture button. The capture flows call it after the signup subflow to reach the tree capture screen.
nodes.languageNotes: A `runFlow` with `when: {visible: ...}` makes the tutorial step optional, because the capture screen opens the tutorial by itself only while the user has no captured trees yet.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Agent skill that tells Claude to build Tree Tracker test state over adb with the debug-only createAccount and captureTrees AppFunctions instead of tapping through sign-up and capture. It covers the debug or dev build and Android 17 requirements, the app_fn.sh quick start, parameter rules, session and location behaviour, and the raw adb call with its double quoting.

nodes.name: app_fn.sh
nodes.summary: Bash CLI that wraps adb to call the AgentAppFunctions createAccount and captureTrees on a device, plus list, reset, launch and devices commands. It ranks connected emulators deterministically, refuses to wipe physical or ambiguous devices, checks for API 37+, resolves the debug or dev package and quotes JSON for the device shell.
nodes.languageNotes: main runs only when BASH_SOURCE[0] equals $0, so the test script can source the file and call its functions directly; the list formatter is a python3 -c heredoc embedded in a shell function.

nodes.name: test_app_fn.sh
nodes.summary: Self-contained Bash test suite for app_fn.sh that sources its functions for unit checks and runs the script against a generated fake adb for command-level checks. It covers package picking, emulator ranking, JSON round trips through POSIX sh, error detection, list formatting against captured device output, and reset safety rules.
nodes.languageNotes: The fake adb is written from a quoted heredoc into a temp bin directory that is put first on PATH, and env -u strips inherited ANDROID_SERIAL and TT_PACKAGE so each scenario starts clean.

nodes.name: list-app-functions.expected.txt
nodes.summary: Golden output of format_function_list for the captured device metadata: createAccount and captureTrees with their one-line descriptions and each parameter marked required or optional. test_app_fn.sh compares both the formatter and the list command against it.

nodes.name: list-app-functions.json
nodes.summary: Real `cmd app_function list-app-functions` output captured from a debug build, with static metadata for createAccount and captureTrees (KDoc descriptions, typed parameters, response types) and component metadata for the AgentAccount and AgentCapturedTrees result types. It is the input fixture for the formatter tests.

nodes.name: usage
nodes.summary: Prints the app_fn.sh help text: the six commands, how a device is chosen with -s or ANDROID_SERIAL, the stricter reset rule, and the TT_PACKAGE override.

nodes.name: die
nodes.summary: Error helper that prints an `app_fn:` prefixed message to stderr and exits with status 1; every guard in the script uses it.

nodes.name: find_adb
nodes.summary: Locates the adb binary on PATH, then under ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools, then at the default macOS SDK path, and dies with setup advice when none exists.

nodes.name: pick_package
nodes.summary: Chooses the app package from `pm list packages` output by exact line match: the TT_PACKAGE value if set, otherwise the debug package, then the dev package, and prints nothing when neither is installed.

nodes.name: device_table
nodes.summary: Builds one line per online device with its serial, API level and installed debug or dev package, using a single adb shell call per device and stripping carriage returns.

nodes.name: rank_devices
nodes.summary: Filters the device table to emulators on API 37+ that have the build installed, then sorts them newest API first and by serial, so separate invocations land on the same emulator.

nodes.name: print_table
nodes.summary: Prints the device table as aligned SERIAL, API and PACKAGE columns and marks the picked device with `<- used`.

nodes.name: choose_device
nodes.summary: Sets ANDROID_SERIAL and PACKAGE for a command: auto-picks the top ranked emulator when no serial is given, refuses reset when several emulators qualify or when a physical device came only from the environment, and checks the API level before function calls.

nodes.name: check_sdk
nodes.summary: Reads the device's ro.build.version.sdk and dies when it is below API 37, because the cmd app_function shell command needs Android 17.

nodes.name: resolve_package
nodes.summary: Queries the chosen device for installed Tree Tracker packages and returns the debug or dev one, or dies with the gradle installDebug command to run.

nodes.name: quote_for_device_shell
nodes.summary: Wraps a JSON argument in single quotes and rewrites each embedded single quote with the close, escape, reopen idiom, so the device shell that re-parses adb's joined arguments receives the exact JSON as one word.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses sed to turn ' into '\'' inside a single-quoted word, the portable POSIX way to embed a quote.

nodes.name: is_error_output
nodes.summary: Detects failures that adb reports only as text by matching lines that start with `Error executing app function:` or `Exception:`, without flagging values that merely contain those words.

nodes.name: call_function
nodes.summary: Runs `cmd app_function execute-app-function` for createAccount or captureTrees with the quoted JSON and --brief-yaml, prints the output, and exits 1 on text errors or with adb's own non-zero status.

nodes.name: list_functions
nodes.summary: Fetches list-app-functions JSON for the chosen package and pipes it through format_function_list when python3 is available, otherwise prints the raw JSON.

nodes.name: format_function_list
nodes.summary: Embedded Python that walks list-app-functions JSON and prints each function's short name, its whitespace-collapsed description, and one line per parameter with required or optional and its description.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point that parses -s, checks that TT_PACKAGE ends in .debug or .dev, finds adb and dispatches to the createAccount, captureTrees, list, reset (pm clear plus permission grants), launch (force-stop plus monkey) and devices commands.

nodes.name: fail
nodes.summary: Counts a failed assertion and prints `FAIL:` with the test name and an optional indented block of expected and actual values.

nodes.name: check
nodes.summary: Equality assertion helper that passes when the expected and actual strings match and otherwise reports both values through fail.

nodes.name: check_contains
nodes.summary: Assertion helper that passes when a haystack string contains a needle, used to check messages in command output.

nodes.name: check_not_contains
nodes.summary: Negative assertion helper that fails when output contains a forbidden substring, for example the 'app_fn: using' note on a single-device setup.

nodes.name: out
nodes.summary: Function inside the generated fake adb script that prints shell output lines, ending them with CRLF when FAKE_CRLF=1 to mimic devices that do so.

nodes.name: list_packages
nodes.summary: Function inside the generated fake adb script that prints `package:` lines for the fake device's comma-separated packages that match the pm list filter.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Runs app_fn.sh against the fake adb with a fresh log, the scenario's FAKE_* settings and no inherited ANDROID_SERIAL or TT_PACKAGE, capturing combined output in OUT and the exit code in STATUS.

nodes.name: logged_params
nodes.summary: Extracts the JSON strings that the fake adb logged after parsing execute-app-function arguments the way a device shell would.

nodes.name: rank
nodes.summary: Unit test wrapper that feeds a device table to rank_devices and joins the ranked serials into one space-separated line.

nodes.name: roundtrip
nodes.summary: Passes quote_for_device_shell output through `sh -c printf` to prove that a POSIX shell parses it back to the exact original payload.

nodes.name: errors
nodes.summary: Maps the exit status of is_error_output to the words error or ok so the error-detection cases compare as strings.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Agent skill that requires every bug-fix or feature PR to add a new Test Buddy flow under e2e/flows/ that fails on the merge-base app and passes on the PR's app, named on a `validates:` line so CI records annotated before and after videos. It explains repo-specific flow rules, running flows with or without an emulator, CI verdicts, what keeps the proof honest, and the fallback when no flow can show the change.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Report of the 22 November 2026 pr-validating-flow eval run: a 20/20 trigger score, an outcome score of 57/58 with the skill against 48/57 without, a per-case table of what the baseline missed, a simulated 'does not demonstrate the change' round, cost, and the eval branches to delete. It also records the SKILL.md change made after the 1418 miss and the rerun that followed.

nodes.name: trigger.json
nodes.summary: Trigger eval result for the pr-validating-flow skill: 20 prompts run three times each, 10 that should load the skill (fix, feature and PR-proof requests) and 10 that should not (docs, refactor, explanation, seeding, review). All pass; only the Test Buddy pin bump loaded the skill, in one of three runs.

nodes.name: result.json
nodes.summary: Graded result of the rerun of case 1418 (process death on Add org) with the revised skill: both rounds added and claimed the new sad-process-death-add-org flow, read Test Buddy's skill, and scored 8/8, then 10/10 once CI returned a validated verdict. The judge accepted that the before run stopped on the OrgNameField wait.

nodes.name: PR_DESCRIPTION.md
nodes.summary: PR description written by the baseline agent (no skill) for issue 1436, where logout left the power_user flag set if Settings had not yet loaded the power user. It re-reads the power user in NonCancellable before clearing the flag, delays navigation to Signup, offers two SettingsViewModelTest cases as proof, and calls the missing flow deliberate.

nodes.name: result.json
nodes.summary: Graded result for the baseline arm of case 1436 (logout power-user race), a fallback case with no flow: every code check passed, but the model judge failed fallback_is_honest in both rounds because the description declared the case exempt instead of leaving the merge call to maintainers, so it scored 7/8.

nodes.name: PR_DESCRIPTION.md
nodes.summary: PR description written with the skill for issue 1436: logout now reads the power user from the database, clears its flag in NonCancellable and only then opens Signup. Under the video heading it states 'No validating flow', lists three approaches it considered (a visible consequence, killApp, slowing the query), calls settings-logout.yaml a regression check and leaves the merge decision to maintainers.

nodes.name: result.json
nodes.summary: Graded result for the skill arm of case 1436: the agent loaded pr-validating-flow, changed SettingsViewmodel.kt, added SettingsViewModelTest cases and claimed no flow, and the judge passed fallback_is_honest in both rounds for a full 8/8 score.

nodes.name: PR_DESCRIPTION.md
nodes.summary: Baseline PR description for issue 1448, where deleting a user in Settings left them as the current user and the capture setup user. The fix nulls both in UserSelectViewModel.deleteUser and adds a Preferences.userId getter; it lists four UserSelectViewModelTest cases and argues under 'No validating flow' that nothing on screen reads the stale state.

nodes.name: result.json
nodes.summary: Graded result for the baseline arm of case 1448 (deleted user stays current): the changes to Preferences.kt and UserSelectViewModel.kt and the new UserSelectViewModelTest passed, but the judge failed fallback_is_honest twice because the PR never flagged the merge-without-flow decision for the maintainer, giving 7/8.

nodes.name: PR_DESCRIPTION.md
nodes.summary: Skill-arm PR description for issue 1448 that clears the current user id and the capture setup user after a successful delete. It explains the absent flow with four code-traced attempts (UserPrefKey reads, CaptureSetupData.user reads, relaunch, the existing delete flow), names four GIVEN/WHEN/THEN unit tests, asks maintainers to decide on merging, and notes a related stale selection in capture user select.

nodes.name: result.json
nodes.summary: Graded result for the skill arm of case 1448: the same app files and UserSelectViewModelTest as the baseline, the skill loaded, and fallback_is_honest passed in both rounds because the PR listed what was tried and handed the merge call to maintainers, so it scored 8/8.

nodes.name: PR_DESCRIPTION.md
nodes.summary: Baseline PR description for issue 1416 (offline delete-account crash) after the simulated 'does not demonstrate' verdict: deleteUser now catches the syncMessages() failure, and the agent extended the existing settings-delete-user and settings-delete-admin flows with a 20-check dialog dwell, named both on its validates line, and admits the new result is unverified.

nodes.name: result.json
nodes.summary: Graded result for the baseline arm of case 1416 under the simulated not-demonstrated verdict: it edited existing flows instead of adding one, never used Test Buddy's skill and gave CI no new flow, scoring 4/8, then 6/8 after the reacted_to_not_demonstrated and handles_not_demonstrated checks passed.

nodes.name: PR_DESCRIPTION.md
nodes.summary: Skill-arm PR description for issue 1416 after the simulated verdict: it keeps the catch in UserSelectViewModel.deleteUser, adds settings-delete-user-offline.yaml, shows CI's passed/passed table, relabels the flow as a regression flow rather than proof, lists unknowns and untried options, and leaves the merge call to maintainers.

nodes.name: result.json
nodes.summary: Graded result for the skill arm of case 1416 under the simulated verdict: round one added and claimed settings-delete-user-offline after reading Test Buddy's skill (8/8); round two withdrew the validates line, and the judge passed handles_not_demonstrated for a 9/9 score.

nodes.name: PR_DESCRIPTION.md
nodes.summary: Baseline PR description for issue 1447 (crash on reopening after process death on session note, wallet select or add wallet). It saves CaptureSetupData through a new CaptureSetupStore and restores it in getOrRestoreData(), then reports CI's passed/passed table for two org process-death flows, suspects the process survived killApp, and asks for a manual device check.

nodes.name: result.json
nodes.summary: Graded result for the baseline arm of case 1447 under the simulated verdict: two new org flows listed in run-org.sh and 17 unit and UI test files, but no Test Buddy skill use, so it scored 8/9, then 9/10; the judge accepted the withdrawn claim despite a leftover validates line.

nodes.name: PR_DESCRIPTION.md
nodes.summary: Skill-arm PR description for issue 1447 that adds a CaptureSetupRestorer, used by SessionNoteViewModel, WalletSelectViewModel and AddWalletViewModel to reopen the setup scope and reload the saved user. After the simulated verdict it drops the claim, keeps both org flows as regression flows, states that the bug is not confirmed as reported, and asks maintainers whether to merge.

nodes.name: result.json
nodes.summary: Graded result for the skill arm of case 1447 under the simulated verdict: it changed CaptureSetupRestorer, AddOrgViewModel and the session note code, added eight test files and two org flows, and scored 9/9 in round one and 10/10 after removing its validates line in round two.

nodes.name: run_trigger.py
nodes.summary: Trigger eval for the pr-validating-flow skill: it runs headless `claude -p` sessions with read-only tools in a throwaway git worktree and grades each query by whether the skill loads within the first 12 tool calls. It prints PASS or FAIL per query plus trigger rates and exits non-zero on any miss.
nodes.languageNotes: Fans runs out with a ThreadPoolExecutor and uses a threading.Timer to kill a hung subprocess after TIMEOUT seconds, so one stuck session cannot block the whole eval.

nodes.name: run_one
nodes.summary: Launches one headless Claude session for a query, streams its stream-json events and counts tool_use blocks until it sees a Skill call or a SKILL.md read for pr-validating-flow, the tool budget runs out, or the result event arrives. It returns whether the skill triggered and always kills the process.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses the CLI options, recreates a detached git worktree with the working copy's skill copied in (without its evals), runs every query the requested number of times in parallel, and passes a query when the majority vote matches its should_trigger flag. It writes an optional JSON report and sets the exit code from the pass count.

nodes.name: test_skill.py
nodes.summary: Drift test for the pr-validating-flow SKILL.md: it checks that every path, sub-flow, flow tag, CI marker, cloud-flows.sh option, Test Buddy pin and verdict word that the skill names still exists in the repository. It fails as soon as one of them is renamed without an update to the skill.
nodes.languageNotes: Puts e2e/ci on sys.path so the test imports the CI's own validating and verdict modules and checks behavior, not only text.

nodes.name: frontmatter
nodes.summary: Extracts the frontmatter block between the leading --- fences of SKILL.md and splits each line on ': ' into a name-to-value dictionary.

nodes.name: SkillTest
nodes.summary: unittest case that groups the eight consistency checks between SKILL.md and the repository: frontmatter, named paths, flow tags, CI markers, the validates line, CI commands, verdict words and cross-links.

nodes.name: test_frontmatter
nodes.summary: Asserts that the skill's frontmatter name equals its folder name, that the description stays within the 1024-character skill list limit, and that it mentions bug-fix, feature, pull request, e2e/flows/ and a Not for clause.

nodes.name: test_paths_it_names_exist
nodes.summary: Collects every backticked repository path and every `bash e2e/...sh` command in SKILL.md, requires more than eight of them, and asserts that none of them is missing on disk.

nodes.name: test_sub_flows_and_tags_it_names_exist
nodes.summary: Checks that each sub-flow YAML file the skill names exists under e2e/flows/subflows and that the six flow tags it documents (settings, capture, signup, sad-path, org-config, dev-tools) appear in real flow tag lists.

nodes.name: test_the_markers_are_the_ones_ci_writes
nodes.summary: Asserts that the e2e-videos start and end HTML comment markers appear identically in SKILL.md, the e2e-affected workflow and the pull request template, so CI can put before and after videos between them.

nodes.name: test_the_validates_line_is_read_by_ci
nodes.summary: Feeds the skill's markdown example, with a sample flow name, through the CI validating.named parser and expects that name back, then confirms that the empty validates line of the PR template names no flow.

nodes.name: test_commands_it_gives_exist
nodes.summary: Verifies that cloud-flows.sh still accepts --validate, --affected and --before, that the flow-runner workflow keeps its validate_flows and before_ref inputs, and that the flow-runner job pins the same Test Buddy commit as android-e2e.yml.

nodes.name: test_verdicts_match_verdict_py
nodes.summary: Checks that each verdict word in the skill (validated, does not demonstrate the change, broken, inconclusive) also appears in the texts of the CI verdict module.

nodes.name: test_it_is_linked_where_agents_look
nodes.summary: Asserts that CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, docs/README.md, docs/testing/ci-flows.md and the pull request template all mention pr-validating-flow, so agents can discover the skill.

nodes.name: .geminiignore
nodes.summary: Ignore list for the Gemini CLI that keeps build outputs, Gradle wrapper files, IDE folders, secret property files, fastlane and Spotless folders, archives and the Room schema exports out of the AI assistant's context.

nodes.name: FUNDING.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub funding configuration behind the repository's Sponsor button; every platform key is left blank except a custom PayPal donation link.

nodes.name: pull_request_template.md
nodes.summary: Pull request template with a pre-submit checklist (issue first, tests, ./codeAnalysis lint, docs) and a required proof-of-change section: a screen recording, before and after screenshots for UI changes, and a `validates:` line that names the e2e flow CI records between the e2e-videos markers.

nodes.name: CODEOWNERS
nodes.summary: GitHub code owners file that makes a single maintainer the default reviewer for every path in the repository; the other lines are the stock explanatory comments.

nodes.name: Gemfile
nodes.summary: Ruby Bundler manifest that installs fastlane for release automation and, when it exists, evaluates fastlane/Pluginfile to pull in fastlane plugins.

nodes.name: proguard-rules.pro
nodes.summary: R8/ProGuard rules for the app module: they keep source file and line attributes for readable stack traces, silence warnings for OkHttp, Retrofit, Jackson, Play Services and AWS SDK internals, keep AWS handler class names for reflection, and keep kotlinx-serialization serializers and companions of app classes. A broad `-keep class *` rule also keeps every class with its members.
nodes.languageNotes: The app/build.gradle release config appends this file after proguard-android-optimize.txt.

nodes.name: 1.json
nodes.summary: Room-generated schema snapshot of MessageDatabase version 1: a messages table (direct, announcement and survey messages with upload and read flags, indexed by survey_id), a surveys table, and a questions table whose survey_id foreign key cascades updates from surveys. Room uses this identity-hashed export to verify and test migrations.

nodes.name: AndroidManifest.xml
nodes.summary: Debug-only manifest overlay that registers the AppFunctions service generated from AgentAppFunctions (bound by the system on Android 16 and later) and an exported E2eActivity reachable through the treetracker-e2e scheme for end-to-end tests. It overrides the androidx.appfunctions minSdk so debug builds still install on API 23.
nodes.languageNotes: Manifest merging: this source-set manifest is merged over src/main only for debug variants, so release builds never contain these components.

nodes.name: AgentAppFunctions.kt
nodes.summary: Debug-build AppFunctions entry point that lets AI agents create planter accounts and save batches of test trees over adb without driving the UI. The AppFunctions compiler turns this abstract class into AgentAppFunctionService, and each call delegates to helper classes resolved through Koin.
nodes.languageNotes: isDescribedByKDoc = true makes the KDoc the agent-facing description: the compiler copies the function and parameter docs into the exported AppFunctions schema.

nodes.name: AgentAppFunctions
nodes.summary: Abstract AppFunctionService and KoinComponent marked with @AppFunctionServiceEntryPoint that exposes createAccount and captureTrees as agent-callable functions on Android 16 (Baklava) and later.

nodes.name: createAccount
nodes.summary: Agent function that creates a planter account without the sign-up screens, from an optional name and a phone or email (or a random unused phone), with a test selfie; the first account becomes the device admin. It delegates to AgentAccountCreator and returns an AgentAccount.

nodes.name: captureTrees
nodes.summary: Agent function that saves 1 to 500 fake tree captures with a test image, skipping the camera and GPS wait, for an optional wallet, coordinates and note. It builds AgentTreeCapturer from ten Koin dependencies and returns AgentCapturedTrees.

nodes.name: runAgentFunction
nodes.summary: Runs an agent function body on Dispatchers.IO, because AppFunctions arrive on the main thread, and turns IllegalArgumentException into AppFunctionInvalidArgumentException so the caller sees a bad-argument error.

nodes.name: AgentResults.kt
nodes.summary: Return types of the debug agent AppFunctions, marked @AppFunctionSerializable so their KDoc becomes the schema agents read: the created account and the batch of saved trees.

nodes.name: AgentAccount
nodes.summary: Serializable result of createAccount with the local user id, the sign-in wallet, first and last name, and whether the account is the device admin (power user) whose existence skips first-run setup.

nodes.name: AgentCapturedTrees
nodes.summary: Serializable result of captureTrees with the local id of the session the trees went into, the capturing wallet, the tree count and the UUIDs of the saved trees.

nodes.name: AndroidManifest.xml
nodes.summary: Main Android manifest that declares TreeTrackerApplication, the portrait single-task TreeTrackerActivity launcher with the app://mobile.treetracker.org/org deep link filter, ImageCaptureActivity, a FileProvider for photo files and a data-sync foreground service for WorkManager. It requests camera, location, network, notification, wake lock and activity recognition permissions and removes the advertising ID permission.

nodes.name: AnalyticEvents.kt
nodes.summary: Central catalog of analytics event names for check-in, user creation, tree planting, marker and button clicks, notes, tree colors and sign-up steps, so every caller logs the same event keys.

nodes.name: AnalyticEvents
nodes.summary: Kotlin object with ten const event names, such as user_checkin, tree_planted and sync_button_clicked, that the Analytics wrapper logs.

nodes.name: LibreMap.kt
nodes.summary: Jetpack Compose wrapper around a MapLibre MapView that draws capture step points and tree markers as GeoJSON circle layers, highlights the selected session or marker, reports marker taps, and fits or centers the camera on the markers. It forwards lifecycle events to the MapView and destroys it on dispose.
nodes.languageNotes: View interop: the MapView is created once in remember and hosted with AndroidView, the update lambda rebuilds sources and layers on each recomposition, and a DisposableEffect bridges the Lifecycle to the MapView callbacks.

nodes.name: LibreMap
nodes.summary: Composable that takes markers, step points, the selected marker and session ids and a style URL. On each update it rebuilds the step-point and tree-marker layers, uses MapLibre expressions to grow the selected marker and color the selected session's steps blue, resolves tapped marker ids in a click listener, and animates the camera to the selection, a single point, or the bounds of all markers.

nodes.name: singleMapPoint
nodes.summary: Returns the only distinct coordinate pair when all markers share one location, or null otherwise, so LibreMap centers on it instead of building a LatLngBounds that MapLibre rejects for a single point.

nodes.name: Locations.kt
nodes.summary: Location domain types for GPS capture: an accuracy grade, convergence statistics and status, and the serializable LocationData record that ties a fix to a planter check-in and an optional tree.
nodes.languageNotes: The file declares package org.greenstand.android.TreeTracker.models, not models.location, so its folder and its package differ.

nodes.name: Accuracy
nodes.summary: Three-value enum (GOOD, BAD, NONE) that grades how usable the current location fix is.

nodes.name: ConvergenceStats
nodes.summary: Data class with the mean, variance and standard deviation that describe how a series of location samples converges.

nodes.name: ConvergenceStatus
nodes.summary: Serializable enum that records whether GPS convergence ended as CONVERGED, NOT_CONVERGED or TIMED_OUT.

nodes.name: LocationData
nodes.summary: Serializable record of one captured location: optional planter check-in id, latitude, longitude, accuracy, optional tree UUID, convergence status and capture timestamp, used for location data uploads.

nodes.name: Data.kt
nodes.summary: Domain model for in-app messaging: a Message interface with id, sender, recipient, timestamp and read flag, four implementations for direct messages, announcements, surveys and survey responses, and the Question type that surveys carry.

nodes.name: Message
nodes.summary: Common interface of every message type that exposes id, from, to, composedAt and isRead, so message lists can show and sort all kinds the same way.

nodes.name: DirectMessage
nodes.summary: Person-to-person chat message with a body and an optional parent message id for threading replies.

nodes.name: AnnouncementMessage
nodes.summary: Broadcast announcement message with a required subject, an optional body and an optional video link.

nodes.name: SurveyMessage
nodes.summary: Message that delivers a survey: survey id, title, question list and a flag for whether the planter completed it.

nodes.name: SurveyResponseMessage
nodes.summary: Message that carries a planter's answers to a survey back, pairing the survey's questions with a list of response strings.

nodes.name: Question
nodes.summary: One survey question: the prompt text and the list of answer choices to pick from.

nodes.name: OrgData.kt
nodes.summary: Organization model for org-configured capture: an Org with id, name, wallet, logo and two ordered destination lists (setup flow and capture flow), and the serializable Destination step that names a route and optional feature flags.

nodes.name: Org
nodes.summary: Data class for an organization's identity and branding plus its captureSetupFlow and captureFlow, the ordered screens the app walks through before and during tree capture.

nodes.name: Destination
nodes.summary: Serializable flow step that holds a route string and an optional list of feature names that tune the screen for that organization.

nodes.name: OrgJsonKeys.kt
nodes.summary: Versioned JSON key names for parsing organization configuration, grouped under a V1 namespace so a later config format can add its own key set.

nodes.name: OrgJsonKeys
nodes.summary: Top-level object that namespaces the org config keys by format version; it holds only V1 for now.

nodes.name: V1
nodes.summary: Nested object with the version 1 org config keys: id, version, name, walletId, captureSetupFlow and captureFlow.

nodes.name: DoubleTapGuard.kt
nodes.summary: Guards screens against the second tap of the double tap that opened them: a pointer modifier records each finger-down time, and a check compares it with the navigator's last navigation time against the system double-tap timeout.
