It covers small screens where the next screen's button sits under the finger.

nodes.name: DoubleTapGuard
nodes.summary: Class with injectable clock and timeout providers; its modifier records the uptime of every finger down on the screen root without consuming it, and its check uses up that press to decide whether a click is a stray double tap.

nodes.name: recordPress
nodes.summary: Stores the uptime of the latest finger down; it is internal so tests can feed presses directly.

nodes.name: isSecondTapOfDoubleTap
nodes.summary: Method that turns the recorded press into milliseconds since the press (0 when there was none, as with the keyboard Go action), clears it, and asks the pure helper with the navigator's millisSinceLastNavigation.

nodes.name: rememberDoubleTapGuard
nodes.summary: Composable that remembers one DoubleTapGuard per composition, so a screen keeps its recorded press across recompositions.

nodes.name: isSecondTapOfDoubleTap
nodes.summary: Pure decision function: false when no navigation happened yet, otherwise true when the press went down within the double-tap timeout of the last navigation, or before it. It uses the press event time, so a tap that reaches a busy device late is still caught.

nodes.name: FlowNavigationController.kt
nodes.summary: Abstract base of the org-configured flow navigators: it tracks the current index into a list of Destination steps, exposes start and end checks, and resolves a step's route string to a typed no-arg Navigation 3 key through RouteRegistry.

nodes.name: FlowNavigationController
nodes.summary: Abstract class that holds the nav path and the current index, with currentDestination, isAtStart and isAtEnd properties and protected index helpers that the capture setup and capture flow controllers build on.

nodes.name: incrementIndex
nodes.summary: Moves to the next step while the index is still inside the path and reports whether it advanced.

nodes.name: decrementIndex
nodes.summary: Steps the index back by one and reports whether it is still zero or more, so a caller can tell that it left the flow.

nodes.name: resetIndex
nodes.summary: Returns the flow to its first step by setting the index back to zero.

nodes.name: resolveNoArgDestination
nodes.summary: Normalizes a Destination's route string and looks it up in RouteRegistry, returning the matching no-arg NavKey, or null for routes that need arguments.

nodes.name: OrgDeepLink.kt
nodes.summary: Parses the organization deep link app://mobile.treetracker.org/org?id=...&name=... from the launch intent into the SplashRoute start destination. It replaces the Navigation 2 navDeepLink that Navigation 3 lacks and runs at cold start only.

nodes.name: parseStartRoute
nodes.summary: Returns a SplashRoute with the org id and name query parameters when the intent URI matches the app scheme, the mobile.treetracker.org host and the /org path prefix, and a plain SplashRoute for any other or missing URI.

nodes.name: Routes.kt
nodes.summary: Typed Navigation 3 route keys for every screen in the app: @Serializable data objects for screens without arguments and data classes for screens that need ids, paths or flags, so the back stack can be saved and restored.
nodes.languageNotes: Each route implements NavKey and is @Serializable; data objects give argument-free screens stable equality and a readable toString.

nodes.name: SplashRoute
nodes.summary: Launch screen route with an optional orgId and orgName, filled from the organization deep link so the splash screen can apply that organization.

nodes.name: SignupFlowRoute
nodes.summary: Argument-free key for the sign-up screen where a new planter registers.

nodes.name: DeleteProfileRoute
nodes.summary: Key for the delete profile screen that Settings opens to remove a planter account.

nodes.name: OrgRoute
nodes.summary: Key for the organization picker screen where the user chooses the organization to capture for.

nodes.name: DashboardRoute
nodes.summary: Key for the home dashboard; the capture and setup flows pop back to it when they end.

nodes.name: TreeHeightScreenRoute
nodes.summary: Key for the tree height screen, one of the steps an organization can add to its capture flow through RouteRegistry.

nodes.name: UserSelectRoute
nodes.summary: Key for the user select screen that picks the planter who starts a capture session; org flows can address it by name.

nodes.name: ProfileSelectRoute
nodes.summary: Key for the screen that Settings opens to choose which planter profile to view or edit.

nodes.name: WalletSelectRoute
nodes.summary: Key for the wallet select step of capture setup, where the planter picks the wallet the session's trees go to.

nodes.name: AddWalletRoute
nodes.summary: Key for the add wallet screen used to enter a new wallet from the wallet select step.

nodes.name: SettingsRoute
nodes.summary: Key for the settings screen with its profile, tree editing and account deletion entries.

nodes.name: SessionNoteRoute
nodes.summary: Key for the session note screen where the planter writes a note for the capture session, a step that organizations can configure.

nodes.name: AddOrgRoute
nodes.summary: Key for the add organization screen of the capture setup flow, which org configuration can address by name.

nodes.name: SelfieRoute
nodes.summary: Key for the selfie camera screen that takes the planter's profile photo during sign-up.

nodes.name: MessagesUserSelectRoute
nodes.summary: Key for the screen that chooses which planter's message inbox to open.

nodes.name: DevOptionsRoute
nodes.summary: Key for the developer options screen with debug toggles and overrides.

nodes.name: MapRoute
nodes.summary: Key for the map screen that plots captured trees and session step points with LibreMap.

nodes.name: TreeEditUserSelectRoute
nodes.summary: Key for the Settings screen that picks a planter before it lists that planter's trees for editing.

nodes.name: ProfileRoute
nodes.summary: Route to one planter's profile screen, identified by planterInfoId.

nodes.name: IndividualMessageListRoute
nodes.summary: Route to the message list of one planter, identified by planterInfoId.

nodes.name: SurveyRoute
nodes.summary: Route to the survey screen of the survey message with the given messageId.

nodes.name: ImageReviewRoute
nodes.summary: Route to the selfie review screen that shows the photo at photoPath so the planter can accept or retake it.

nodes.name: LanguageRoute
nodes.summary: Route to the language selection screen; isFromTopBar (true by default) tells it whether the top bar button opened it.

nodes.name: TreeCaptureRoute
nodes.summary: Route to the tree capture camera screen that passes the planter's profilePicUrl for display in the capture UI.

nodes.name: TreeImageReviewRoute
nodes.summary: Route to the tree photo review step of the capture flow; it carries photoPath, but the navigation host builds the screen without reading it.

nodes.name: ChatRoute
nodes.summary: Route to a direct-message chat between the planter with planterInfoId and the other party named by otherChatIdentifier.

nodes.name: AnnouncementRoute
nodes.summary: Route to the announcement detail screen of the message with the given messageId.

nodes.name: TreeListRoute
nodes.summary: Route to the editable list of one planter's trees, keyed by userWallet and titled with userName.

nodes.name: TreeDetailRoute
nodes.summary: Route to the detail and edit screen of one tree, identified by its local database treeId.

nodes.name: TreeTrackerTheme.kt
nodes.summary: App-wide Material theme composable that applies the project Colors palette, default typography and 12 dp rounded small shapes to its content. The file sits in theme/ but declares the view package.

nodes.name: TreeTrackerTheme
nodes.summary: Composable wrapper around MaterialTheme that screens and previews use to get the shared colors, typography and rounded small-component shapes.

nodes.name: UseCase.kt
nodes.summary: Generic base of the app's use case classes: one suspend execute method that takes typed parameters and returns a typed result, which gives sync, upload and tree creation logic one calling convention.
nodes.languageNotes: Declaration-site variance: Params is contravariant (in) and Result is covariant (out).

nodes.name: UseCase
nodes.summary: Abstract generic class with a contravariant Params and a covariant Result that use cases such as SyncDataUseCase and CreateTreeUseCase extend.

nodes.name: execute
nodes.summary: Abstract suspend entry point that each use case implements to do its work with the given params and return its result.

nodes.name: StringExtensions.kt
nodes.summary: Adds String extension functions that turn text into hexadecimal digests: a dedicated MD5 helper and a generic hashString that accepts any MessageDigest algorithm name.

nodes.name: md5
nodes.summary: Computes the MD5 digest of the receiver string and returns it as lowercase hex with zero-padded bytes; if the MD5 algorithm is missing it logs through Timber and returns an empty string.

nodes.name: hashString
nodes.summary: Hashes the receiver string with the named MessageDigest algorithm (for example SHA-256) and encodes each byte as two uppercase hex characters through a nibble lookup table.

nodes.name: StateExtentions.kt
nodes.summary: Provides two inline updateState extensions that apply a copy-style transform to the current UI state, one for MutableStateFlow and one for MutableLiveData, so view models can update immutable state in one call.
nodes.languageNotes: Both overloads share the name updateState and differ only by receiver type, so Kotlin picks the overload from the receiver. The file name keeps the original 'Extentions' spelling.

nodes.name: updateState
nodes.summary: Replaces the value of a MutableStateFlow synchronously with the result of a lambda that receives the current state as its receiver.

nodes.name: updateState
nodes.summary: Posts a transformed copy of a MutableLiveData value, which is safe from any thread, and fails fast with the message 'Must have state' when the LiveData has no value yet.

nodes.name: Utils.kt
nodes.summary: Holds a coroutine helper that runs a suspend action for every element of a list concurrently on a chosen dispatcher and waits until all of them finish.

nodes.name: runInParallel
nodes.summary: Starts one async job per list item inside withContext (Dispatchers.IO by default) and awaits each job in order, so the call returns only after every action completes and rethrows the first failure.

nodes.name: ActionButtons.kt
nodes.summary: Defines the square approve or decline button and the round info button used on review screens and dialogs, both built on TreeTrackerButton with drawable icons and stable test tags for UI tests.

nodes.name: ApprovalButton
nodes.summary: Renders a 60 dp TreeTrackerButton with a green check icon for approval or a red close icon for decline, and tags it ApproveButton or DeclineButton unless a dialog passes its own test tag.

nodes.name: InfoButton
nodes.summary: Renders a 60 dp white circular TreeTrackerButton with the info icon and the InfoButton test tag; its shape parameter is accepted but ignored, so the button is always a circle.

nodes.name: CaptureButtons.kt
nodes.summary: Provides the orange add button and the green camera capture button, plus a Canvas-drawn shutter icon that the capture button shows on its face.

nodes.name: OrangeAddButton
nodes.summary: Shows a 70 dp circular orange TreeTrackerButton with an add icon and the OrangeAddButton test tag, for screens that offer an add action.

nodes.name: CaptureButton
nodes.summary: Shows a 70 dp circular green TreeTrackerButton with a deeper press travel that wraps an ImageCaptureCircle shutter icon, and honours an isEnabled flag so callers can block a capture.

nodes.name: ImageCaptureCircle
nodes.summary: Draws a camera shutter glyph on a Canvas: a filled circular background in the main color, then an outlined ring and a solid inner dot in the shadow color.

nodes.name: Colors.kt
nodes.summary: Central color palette of the Compose UI: AppColors holds the raw brand colors with shadow and disabled variants, AppButtonColors pairs them into DepthButtonColors sets for 3D buttons, and the file also defines a dark Material Colors theme and a swatch preview.
nodes.languageNotes: Kotlin object declarations are lazily created singletons, so AppColors and AppButtonColors give app-wide constant palettes without dependency injection.

nodes.name: AppColors
nodes.summary: Singleton of named Color constants (grays, green, purple, red, yellow, sky blue, orange and the two message bubble colors), with shadow and disabled variants where depth buttons need them.

nodes.name: AppButtonColors
nodes.summary: Singleton of ready-made DepthButtonColors presets (Default, WhiteLight, ProgressGreen, DeclineRed, MessagePurple, UploadOrange, Yellow, SkyBlue) that map face, shadow and disabled colors for TreeTrackerButton.

nodes.name: ColorPalettePreview
nodes.summary: Android Studio preview that lays out the AppColors swatches in rows by hue; the green row reuses the gray labels, so its captions do not match the colors shown.

nodes.name: Palette
nodes.summary: Private composable that paints one 100 dp swatch in the given color and prints the swatch name and its uppercase ARGB hex code on it.

nodes.name: Containers.kt
nodes.summary: Supplies fixed 70 dp rounded-corner containers for thumbnails, including a variant that loads and center-crops a photo from a local file path.

nodes.name: RoundedImageContainer
nodes.summary: Clips any composable content to a 70 by 70 dp box with 10 dp rounded corners, and applies the caller modifier after the built-in size and clip.

nodes.name: RoundedLocalImageContainer
nodes.summary: Fills a RoundedImageContainer with a center-cropped LocalImage loaded from the given file path, which gives a ready-made photo thumbnail.

nodes.name: Images.kt
nodes.summary: Loads photos stored on the device into Compose: a LocalImage composable with a dark gray placeholder and a loader that decodes the file into an ImageBitmap state.

nodes.name: LocalImage
nodes.summary: Displays the bitmap decoded from a local image path with the requested ContentScale, and shows a placeholder composable (a dark gray box by default) while the bitmap is missing.

nodes.name: loadLocalImage
nodes.summary: Returns a Compose State that starts as null and later receives the BitmapFactory-decoded ImageBitmap for the path; decode errors are swallowed, so a bad file leaves the state null.

nodes.name: Loading.kt
nodes.summary: Holds the progress indicators of the app: a full-screen centered green spinner for loading states and a Canvas-drawn orange ring that fills in proportion to a progress value.

nodes.name: showLoadingSpinner
nodes.summary: Overlays a 70 dp green CircularProgressIndicator at the center of a full-size box when isLoading is true, and renders nothing otherwise.

nodes.name: DeterminateProgressBar
nodes.summary: Draws a circular progress ring on a Canvas with an 8 dp butt-capped stroke: a gray full-circle track and an orange arc from 180 degrees that sweeps progress times 360 degrees, with progress semantics for accessibility.

nodes.name: NavigationButtons.kt
nodes.summary: Defines the back and forward arrow buttons that flow screens place in their bottom bar, built on TreeTrackerButton and centered inside a BoxScope.

nodes.name: ArrowButton
nodes.summary: BoxScope extension composable that centers a 62 dp TreeTrackerButton (green by default) with a back or forward arrow icon and the matching ArrowBackButton or ArrowForwardButton test tag.

nodes.name: arrowPainter
nodes.summary: Private composable helper that returns the arrow_backward or the arrow_forward drawable painter, chosen by the isLeft flag.

nodes.name: TextButton.kt
nodes.summary: Implements TreeTrackerButton, the base 3D push button of the app: a still shadow layer and a face layer that slides down when pressed, with haptic feedback, accessibility semantics, and rectangle or circle shapes.
nodes.languageNotes: The circle branch calls aspectRatio(1f) inside modifier.apply { }. Compose modifiers are immutable values, so the returned modifier is discarded and the aspect ratio is never applied.

nodes.name: TreeTrackerButton
nodes.summary: Draws a depth button whose face moves down by an animated top padding (100 ms tween) while pressed or selected, calls onClick with LongPress haptics on tap, and exposes one merged Button node with enabled and selected state to screen readers and UI test tools.

nodes.name: TreeTrackerButtonShape
nodes.summary: Enum that selects the outline of a TreeTrackerButton: Rectangle uses the small Material shape, and Circle uses CircleShape with a start offset equal to the button depth.

nodes.name: TreeTrackerButtonPreview
nodes.summary: Android Studio preview that renders one rectangular and one circular TreeTrackerButton inside TreeTrackerTheme on a gray 200 by 300 dp column.

nodes.name: ic_launcher.xml
nodes.summary: Adaptive launcher icon for Android 8.0 and later (API 26+) that layers the ic_launcher_foreground mipmap over the white ic_launcher_background color; the manifest uses it as the app icon.

nodes.name: ic_launcher_round.xml
nodes.summary: Round launcher icon variant for API 26+ launchers that repeats the foreground mipmap and background color layers of the standard adaptive icon and backs the roundIcon attribute of the manifest.

nodes.name: strings.xml
nodes.summary: Portuguese translations of all 152 app strings: sync status, sign-up and login hints, permission rationales, GPS help, settings, profile and account deletion dialogs, tree editing labels, name validation errors, and a full Portuguese privacy policy.
nodes.languageNotes: Many entries carry translatable="false". That attribute only has meaning in the default values folder, so inside values-pt it has no effect.

nodes.name: strings.xml
nodes.summary: Swahili translations of the 152 app strings, including sync messages, sign-up fields, permission prompts, GPS troubleshooting steps, profile and account dialogs, tree list labels, and an HTML-formatted Swahili privacy policy.
nodes.languageNotes: The file starts with a UTF-8 byte order mark before the XML declaration, and its privacy policy uses inline <b> and <a> tags that Android keeps as styled text.

nodes.name: locales_config.xml
nodes.summary: Declares the per-app language list (English, Swahili and Portuguese) that Android 13 and later shows in the system app-language settings; the manifest points to it through android:localeConfig.

nodes.name: provider_paths.xml
nodes.summary: FileProvider path map that names the root of external storage external_files, so the FileProvider declared in the manifest can issue content URIs for files below it.

nodes.name: AgentInputTest.kt
nodes.summary: Parameterized JUnit suite for AgentInput, the debug-build checker that validates and normalizes what agents pass to the app's AppFunctions. Nested classes cover name, phone and email rules that match sign-up's messages, wallet lookup variants, tree counts of 1 to 500, optional tree-center coordinates, and longitude wrapping, including a 10,000-sample random sweep.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses JUnit 4's Enclosed runner so each nested class can use its own runner (Parameterized with a @JvmStatic companion cases() factory, or the default).

nodes.name: ValidNames
nodes.summary: Parameterized cases showing that AgentInput.accountDetails accepts and trims Latin, accented, Cyrillic, Arabic and Chinese names up to 50 characters for both first and last name.

nodes.name: InvalidPhones

nodes.name: InvalidEmails

nodes.name: AccountCombinations
nodes.summary: Plain tests for accountDetails argument combinations: the Test User defaults, phone and email passed together, and the order in which fields are checked.

nodes.name: WalletLookups

nodes.name: TreeCounts

nodes.name: ValidTreeCenters

nodes.name: InvalidTreeCenters
nodes.summary: Parameterized cases where treeCenter rejects half-given pairs, out-of-range values, NaN and infinities with precise messages.

nodes.name: NormalizedCoordinates
nodes.summary: Parameterized cases for normalizeCoordinates that clamp latitude to the poles and wrap longitude into the range from -180 up to, but not including, 180.

nodes.name: NormalizedCoordinatesSweep
nodes.summary: Property-style tests that push random and extreme longitudes through normalizeCoordinates and check range and whole-turn equivalence.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Index of the repository's documentation that links getting-started, product, engineering, testing, release, collaboration and process pages plus the PR validating-flow skill. Its two Process links (task workflow and a tasks directory index) point to files that are not in the repository.

nodes.name: meeting-notes.md
nodes.summary: Legacy notes from a January 2021 product meeting that list the topics discussed: signup defaults and wallet selection, selfie confirmation, village coordinator trust and anti-fraud checks, check-in cadence, low-literacy hints and the session data model. They are marked as historical.

nodes.name: releases.md
nodes.summary: Release guide that explains how version codes are set: release and local builds use baseVersionCode from app/build.gradle, while other CI builds add the workflow run number. It also keeps legacy release notes from 1.2.7 to 2.1, including the 2.0.0 Jetpack Compose overhaul.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Task record for bug #1421, where Next on Add org crashed with 'CaptureSetupScope not open' after the camera rationale was cancelled. It explains the fix (the setup scope stays open when capture opens and endSession closes it), the tests and e2e flow, and review follow-ups left open.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Task record for bug #1422, where Next after a system back from Add org skipped Add org because the setup controller's step index was stale. The fix re-derives the index from the back stack in navForward and navFromNewUserCreation; the review follow-ups, unit tests and e2e flow are listed.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Task record for bug #1423, double-tapping Next on user select skipping Add org. It covers the same-screen navForward guard with Navigator.canNavigate, the cross-screen DoubleTapGuard driven by press event times, what CI's 320x640 emulator revealed, the tests, and items left for follow-up.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Task record for a stale UserSelectViewModel that was reused after leaving capture by the profile button and left the setup scope closed. It traces the Navigation 3 ViewModelStore behaviour, the failing UI test written first, and the resumeSetup fix called from a LaunchedEffect.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Task record for #1442, where a double tap on Next skipped org-configured setup steps (session note, wallet select, add wallet). The fix applies the existing DoubleTapGuard to those screens; it lists the Robolectric UI test, an e2e flow for the session-note org, and the review findings.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Task record for crashes after process death on the session note, wallet select and add wallet setup steps. It introduces the shared CaptureSetupRestorer (reopen the scope, reload the saved user) with restoring and setupLost states, and lists its unit, UI and e2e tests and known limits.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Task record for a dependency cleanup that removed deprecated libraries and a dead Maven repository and bumped Gson, Timber, JUnit, Detekt, Room testing and the AndroidX test libraries, with tables of old and new versions and the build checks run.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Task record for #1449: the H1 location-denied e2e flow also passed when the app closed. It shows the gap with a temporary breaking commit and strengthens the flow to wait up to 30 seconds for the language select screen before it checks that the splash is gone.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Task record for org link overrides on the debug dev options screen. It describes OrgOverrides (catalog, merge rules, JSON store), OrgRepo.currentOrg versus baseCurrentOrg, the new Org Link Overrides section in dev options, and the tests that cover them.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Task record for profile name edits that never reached production. It traces the upload path through UserRepo.updateUser and PlanterUploader, fixes the wallet copied into both phone and email and the stale photo URL, and lists related backend issues that this change does not fix.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Task record for a reusable CI flow runner that cloud sessions without an emulator can start on any PR. It lists the flow-runner workflows, the run-flows, step screenshot, summary and cloud-flows scripts, and how each was checked.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Task record for annotated videos of the e2e flows a PR affects. It records the design decisions (flows picked by shared test tag ids, at most six per PR, manual runs for fork PRs) and the new e2e-affected workflow, flow selector scripts and reusable runner job.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Task record that traces lost e2e recordings to emulator adb connection drops on the first pulls after boot and adds a pull warm-up, a re-run and lost-recording reporting to run-flows. It also records part B, the before/after validating-flow check with its verdicts, and other CI findings.

nodes.name: plan.md
nodes.summary: Plan for parts B to D of task 115: picking validating flows, running each on the merge-base app and on the PR app with a pure-code verdict table, options for generating flows (in CI or at authoring time), and inline GIF playback of the recordings in PR comments.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Task record for the pr-validating-flow agent skill and its eval: guidance for writing a flow that fails before and passes after a fix, before/after videos written into the PR description, a manual before/after mode in flow-runner and cloud-flows, and open questions for maintainers.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Records the completed switch from Gson to kotlinx-serialization: Retrofit now uses the kotlinx converter, 19 API models gain @Serializable and @SerialName, the uploaders and OrgRepo encode through the shared Json instance, and the Room converters store null maps as SQL NULL. The motivation is that Gson ignores Kotlin nullability; 208 unit tests passed afterwards.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Describes how Roborazzi screenshot testing came in: a ScreenshotTest base class that hides the Robolectric and theme boilerplate, 18 screens split into a ViewModel-aware root composable and a stateless UI composable, and 18 test classes with 40 golden-image variants. It also adds verifyRoborazziDebug to pull request CI and lists the camera and map screens that stay untested.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Short note on breaking the large DashboardScreen.kt layout into named section composables (DashboardHeader, DashboardStats, SyncStatusSection, DashboardActions) while Dashboard keeps the wiring. It explains why the Column weights moved to the call sites after Compose API changes broke weight resolution inside the children.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Outlines the tree editing feature reached from Settings, where a grower goes through user select and a tree list to a tree detail screen that edits the note or deletes the tree. It lists the five new treeedit screens and ViewModels plus the DAO queries, routes, settings menu entry and strings added for it.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Analyzes the release-blocking Resources$NotFoundException crash on the splash screen (issue #1176) and traces it to a duplicate unqualified splash.png that clashed with the density buckets under AAB splits. The fix deletes that default drawable and wraps painterResource in runCatching with a plain background fallback and a Timber log.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Design and change record for routing one-shot UI signals (snackbars, navigation, dialogs) through a single UiEvent stream from ViewModel to Composable. BaseViewModel swaps its Channel for a replaying MutableSharedFlow guarded by ConsumableEvent, and a SnackbarController provided at Root through a CompositionLocal replaces the per-screen snackbar hosts in Dashboard, TreeDetail and Survey.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Follow-up to the UiEvent work that moves navigation into the ViewModels: PopBackStackEvent replaces NavigateUpEvent and BaseViewModel gains throttled navigate and popBackStack helpers. Survey, TreeDetail and TreeImageReview drop their navigation flags, Settings, Announcement, DevOptions and OrgPicker route nav actions through handleAction, and the callback-driven and capture-chain screens are left for later.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Brief fix note for issue #1231, where LocationDataCapturer made a new MainScope for every location update and never cancelled it. The class now owns one CoroutineScope, cancels pending inserts in stopGpsUpdates(), and has a regression test showing that late inserts no longer land.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Small copy fix for issue #1272 that corrects the misspelled brand name in the English Privacy Policy settings text and aligns the Portuguese and Swahili translations on the GreenStand capitalization, checked with the Settings screenshot test.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Notes the split of the oversized view/TextButton.kt: TreeTrackerButton and its shape enum stay, while the navigation, action, capture, language and user image buttons and DepthButtonColors move to focused files. Its heading still says Task 18, and the Kotlin compile check could not run without a Java runtime.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Detailed record of the move from Jetpack Navigation 2 to Navigation 3: all 29 routes become NavKey, an app-owned Navigator with a NavOptions DSL and 300 ms throttling replaces NavHostController, Host.kt renders a NavDisplay with per-entry ViewModel scoping, and the org deep link is parsed by hand. It also covers the Compose and compileSdk bump and a launch crash fixed by planting a NavigationEventDispatcherOwner.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Explains why installs from 1.x releases crashed with a missing 6 to 9 migration after AutoMigration(7, 8) was dropped, backed by a table of which schema shipped in which release. The fix restores that auto migration, moves the database setup into AppDatabase.builder, and adds a Robolectric test that upgrades a seeded schema 6 database and keeps its unsynced trees.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Describes debug-only AndroidX AppFunctions that let testing agents create accounts and capture batches of trees over adb, without the camera, GPS wait or review screens. It covers the AgentAppFunctions, AgentAccountCreator, AgentTreeCapturer and AgentInput classes, the createSession and closeSession split in SessionTracker, the device helper script and its tests, the alpha08 version choice, and fixes from several review rounds.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Upgrades the toolchain so the project builds on JDK 25: Gradle 9.5.1, AGP 8.13.2, a detekt 2.0 alpha with a migrated detekt.yml that keeps the same limits, and MockK 1.14.11 so File and Runtime can be mocked again. CI moves its setup-java steps to Temurin 25, while the app keeps compiling to Java 11 bytecode.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Repairs the failing Firebase beta deploy by computing CI version codes as baseVersionCode 197 plus the workflow run number, instead of committing a bump to master that could no longer be pushed directly. It documents the build-apk output, the removed bump workflows, why a commit-count scheme was rejected, and the cases where a non-release code can go down.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Plan and outcome of a broad coverage push: a ComposeUiTest base class, a plain-Application Robolectric config, and unit or Compose UI tests across navigation, ViewModels, persistence, sync, domain logic, orgs and every screen. It also lists behavior-preserving extractions of stateless composables and a long catalogue of unfixed bugs found while writing the tests.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Small cleanup for the coverage pull request (#1374) that makes ImageUtilsBitmapTest check the file length, because Robolectric's decodeFile leaves an empty file behind, and ignores the .kotlin/ compiler session folder.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Second coverage round after PR #1374, split into data layer, logic, capture and map UI, and account and shared UI areas, adding about 310 cases such as ManualMigrationsTest, DaoConflictAndIntegrityTest, KoinGraphTest and RoutesSerializationTest. It ends with eight app bugs the tests exposed, including the fixed-size survey answer array and text-sorted timestamps.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Introduces the Android end-to-end CI check: android-e2e.yml builds the tb runner and the debug app, boots a cached API 35 emulator, runs the YAML flows in e2e/flows and uploads a JUnit report with debug artifacts. The first flow checks that a fresh install opens on the language picker.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Prepares every screen for tb end-to-end flows: test tags are centralized in view/TestTags.kt and exposed as resource ids on each composition root, TreeTrackerButton gets real button semantics, and dialogs and repeated items get unique tags. It adds a manually triggered screen tour workflow and lists what still needs camera, GPS or a newer emulator API.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Very short note about writing the end-to-end flow test plan: a navigation map of 29 routes, today's coverage, about 50 proposed happy and sad path flows in 9 groups, and likely bugs. It links the plan from the docs index and the testing guide and changes no code.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Records raising targetSdk to 36 for Google Play and the behavior changes that came with it: camera rotation on large screens, selfie preview sizing, edge-to-edge padding, and sync that survives WorkManager cancellation. It also covers the AppFunctions 1.0.0-rc01 port to a generated service and the AGP 9.1.1 built-in Kotlin setup.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Stops end-to-end flows from crashing at the selfie step by starting the CI emulator with emulated front and back cameras and renaming the AVD snapshot cache key. It notes that Camera.kt still crashes on a device that lacks the requested camera.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Lists the twelve tb flows for first run and signup (A1 to A6) and tree capture (B1 to B6), with shared signup and start-capture subflows, each starting from a fresh install and selecting only by test-tag ids. It records the CustomSnackbar tag change, runs on API 35 emulators, and signup and back navigation bugs found on the way.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Adds tb flows for returning users and settings, sad paths such as denied permissions, process death and double taps, and org-configured variants, plus seed-org.sh and run-org.sh to seed orgs offline. It tracks nine known-bug flows against their issues and explains the CI fixes for airplane mode and pinning tb v0.5.2.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Task note for issue #1415: after logout and sign-in as an existing user, system back on the Dashboard returned to Signup, because `popUpTo<LanguageRoute>` popped nothing on a stack that held only Signup. It records the fix (`navigateToDashboardAfterSignup` with `popUpToRoot()`), the `SignupNavigationTest` cases, and the updated logout e2e flows.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Task note for issue #1416: deleting a user while offline crashed the app, because the message upload in `MessagesRepo.syncMessages()` threw outside any catch. It explains why the try/catch sits in `UserSelectViewModel.deleteUser` (so `SyncDataUseCase` still sees failed uploads) and lists the unit test, the delete-user e2e flows, and the follow-ups left open.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Task note for issue #1417: a location denial at first launch left the app stuck on the splash image. It describes the `SplashScreen` change to always bootstrap and navigate, the review fixes so that `LocationDataCapturer` marks GPS as on only when updates really start and `LocationUpdateManager` catches `SecurityException`, and the updated Robolectric and e2e tests.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Task note for issue #1418: process death on the Add org screen crashed with `CaptureSetupScope not open` after Navigation 3 restored the back stack. It records how `AddOrgViewModel` persists the setup user id, reopens the scope behind a `restoring` state, falls back to the Dashboard when the user is gone, and which setup data is still lost.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Task note for issue #1419: process death on image review crashed, because the capture flow scope, the tree being captured and the session id lived only in memory. It documents the new `PendingTreeStore`, `CaptureFlowScopeManager.restoreAt`, `CaptureFlowNavigationController.resumeAt`, the `AppModule` wiring for the review and tree height view models, and the unit and e2e coverage.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Task note for issue #1420: after process death on the capture screen, GPS updates, the session id and the step and orientation sensors were gone. It describes how `TreeCaptureViewModel` now resumes an interrupted session and starts GPS when it is created, how the branch was reconciled with the #1417 and #1419 fixes on master, and the review gaps left open.

nodes.name: summarize.py
nodes.summary: Turns a run-flows.sh output folder into summary.json and summary.md: one record per flow from results.tsv (status, time, cut step count, error, ordered screenshots, video parts, recording outcome) plus GitHub run details from the environment. It prints the Markdown table so that CI can show it as the run summary and an agent can open one file to find every artifact.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses an assignment expression (`:=`) inside a list comprehension to filter and capture regex matches in one pass.

nodes.name: video_parts
nodes.summary: Finds the numbered video segments `<name>-partN.mp4` that a flow leaves when its recording parts could not be joined, sorted by part number. The anchored regex keeps another flow's `-partial` file out of the list.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Reads results.tsv row by row, pads the optional cut, recording, tries and reason columns, and collects each flow's screenshots (failure shots last), error text, video and captions. It then writes summary.json and a Markdown table with pass and fail counts, a video column only when recording was asked for, and notes for errors and for lost or partial recordings.

nodes.name: test_cloud_flows.py
nodes.summary: Offline unittest suite for the `run` command of e2e/ci/cloud-flows.sh, which dispatches the cloud flow runner workflow. It builds a local bare origin, a fix branch and a fake results branch, and puts a stub `gh` on PATH that logs each call and fails the first status poll, to check the dispatch inputs and the printed verdict.

nodes.name: CloudFlowsRunTest
nodes.summary: Test case that checks what cloud-flows.sh asks GitHub to start: a validate run sends the flow name and a before ref (the merge base by default, or a given ref), a plain run sends no validate inputs, a run with nothing to do exits with status 2, and a 404 on the first poll is waited out.

nodes.name: setUp
nodes.summary: Builds the fixture for each test: a bare origin with master and a `fix` branch one commit ahead, a `flow-results/run-4242` branch that holds summary and verdict files, and a bin directory with the stub `gh` first on PATH and a 1 second poll interval.

nodes.name: test_validate_starts_a_before_and_after_run_and_prints_the_verdict
nodes.summary: Main scenario: `run --validate my-flow` must dispatch on the fix branch with `validate_flows` and the merge base sha as `before_ref`, keep polling after the stub's first 404, print the completed status and the verdict row, and download the verdict file into the output folder.

nodes.name: test_description_block.py
nodes.summary: Tests the github-script of the `comment` job in the e2e-affected workflow, which writes a before and after video table into the PR description between the e2e-videos markers and posts a PR comment. It extracts the script from the workflow YAML and runs it under node with a fake GitHub client, so the tests cover the code that CI really runs; the suite skips when node is missing.
nodes.languageNotes: The embedded JavaScript harness builds an AsyncFunction from the script text to imitate how actions/github-script injects `github`, `context` and `core`.

nodes.name: workflow_script
nodes.summary: Pulls the inline `script: |` body of the `comment` job out of .github/workflows/e2e-affected.yml by scanning lines and indentation, and returns the JavaScript as text for the node harness.

nodes.name: DescriptionBlockTest
nodes.summary: Test case for the PR description block: it replaces stale content between the markers and keeps the text around them, changes nothing on a second identical run, appends the block when markers are absent, shows a no-validating-flow note, never yields a `validates:` line, and leaves a description near the GitHub length limit alone with a warning.

nodes.name: run_script
nodes.summary: Builds a temporary results folder with a verdict.json and before and after GIF stubs, writes the extracted script, the node harness and the env inputs, runs node, and returns the new PR body (or None when no update happened) together with the recorded GitHub API calls.

nodes.name: test_fills_the_marked_block_and_keeps_the_rest
nodes.summary: Checks a full fill: the stale marked block becomes a Validated block that embeds both GIFs and links both MP4s at the results commit, shows the assertion error and the record and annotate hint, keeps the intro and outro text, and creates the comment before it updates the PR.

nodes.name: test_run_flows.py
nodes.summary: Unittest suite for e2e/ci/run-flows.sh that swaps in stub adb and device automation CLIs to test name@N flow cuts, the ANNOTATE option, retries after lost recordings, the adb pull warm-up, and bash 3.2 compatibility. It also reads the summary.json and summary.md that each run leaves behind.

nodes.name: RunFlowsTest
nodes.summary: Test case for the selector and recording rules of run-flows.sh: a whole flow wins over its cuts and the longest cut wins, bad cut selectors exit 2, lost recordings rerun up to RECORD_TRIES and exit 3 when every try fails, a failed flow outranks a lost video, and the script avoids syntax that needs bash 4.

nodes.name: run_flows
nodes.summary: Creates a temporary bin directory with the given stub adb and automation CLI, runs run-flows.sh against a fake emulator serial from the project root, and returns the result, the stub's call log lines, and optionally what a reader extracts from the output folder.

nodes.name: test_cut_whole_and_two_cuts
nodes.summary: Verifies how selectors merge: `signup-back` given whole and cut runs whole, two cuts of settings-logout keep the longer five-step copy, capture-exit@2 runs a two-step copy, and no temporary `.ci-cut-` flow files stay in e2e/flows afterwards.

nodes.name: test_a_lost_recording_runs_the_flow_again
nodes.summary: Checks that a recording lost on the first try makes run-flows.sh run the flow a second time, that the summary marks the video as saved on try 2 with no error, and that the console log of the first try is kept.

nodes.name: test_a_recording_lost_every_time_is_said_and_fails_the_run
nodes.summary: Checks that a recording lost on all three default tries ends the run with status 3, keeps the flow as passed but with recording lost and the adb pull reason, counts it in recordingsLost, and reports it in the Markdown summary and as a GitHub warning annotation.

nodes.name: steps.sh
nodes.summary: Ordered list of tour steps, sourced by tour.sh: it launches the debug app with cleared state and walks language selection, phone signup, the selfie and its tutorial, the dashboard top bar and dev options, every Settings screen, messages, one tree capture with a note, and the new tree in tree edit and on the map, with a snapshot of each screen. Fallback tap positions suit a 1080x2400 Pixel 6 screen.

nodes.name: tour.sh
nodes.summary: Driver for the screen tour of the debug Treetracker app: it defines a small step vocabulary over the device automation CLI, sources steps.sh, and saves the look text, screenshot and view hierarchy of every screen to build/tour. Taps try the test tag first and fall back to a position or text, and a failed step is counted but does not stop the tour.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `set -u` without `set -e` on purpose, so each helper returns a status that callers chain with `&&` and `||` while the walk continues.

nodes.name: snap
nodes.summary: Captures the current screen as the next numbered tour entry: the look text, a PNG screenshot and the JSON view hierarchy, named with a zero-padded counter and the screen label, and copies the look text into tour.log.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Executes one automation command through the CLI's `do` subcommand, logs it, and counts a failure unless OPTIONAL is set. It returns the command's exit status so that callers can chain fallbacks.

nodes.name: tap
nodes.summary: Taps an element by its test tag id. If that fails, it falls back to a screen point when the fallback has a percent sign, or to visible text otherwise, so one tour works on builds with and without test tags.

nodes.name: hold
nodes.summary: Long-presses an element by id, with a screen point as the fallback. The tour uses it on the top bar logo to open the developer options.

nodes.name: wait_id
nodes.summary: Waits until an element with the given id is visible, with a default timeout of 15 seconds that callers raise for slow screens such as image review.

nodes.name: maybe_id
nodes.summary: Waits for an id that may correctly not appear, such as the first-capture review tutorial, by running wait_id with OPTIONAL set, so a timeout does not count as a failed step.

nodes.name: back_to
nodes.summary: Presses the bottom bar back arrow up to three times until the look output lists the target id, and stops early on the dashboard, which has no back arrow. If the id never shows, it counts a failure and logs the last look.

nodes.name: open_settings
nodes.summary: Goes back to the dashboard with back_to, opens Settings from the top bar, and waits for the Profile entry, so the next steps start from a known screen.

nodes.name: type_in
nodes.summary: Focuses a text field by tapping its id (with an optional text fallback) and then enters the given text with an inputText command.

nodes.name: Appfile
nodes.summary: Fastlane app identity file that sets the Android package name `org.greenstand.android.TreeTracker` and leaves the path of the Play Store service account JSON key empty for each maintainer to fill in.

nodes.name: Fastfile
nodes.summary: Fastlane lanes for the Android app: run the unit tests, bump the versionCode in app/build.gradle and push, ship a beta through Firebase App Distribution with Slack notices, and deploy a release to Google Play. A before_all hook refuses to run on a dirty git tree; no workflow in .github/workflows calls these lanes.
nodes.languageNotes: Ruby DSL. bump_version_code matches `versionCode\s+(\d+)`, but app/build.gradle now computes `versionCode = baseVersionCode + offset`, so the regex finds no literal number and the version lanes look out of date.

nodes.name: before_all
nodes.summary: Fastlane hook that runs before every lane and stops the lane unless the git working tree is clean, and shows the uncommitted changes when it is not.

nodes.name: test
nodes.summary: Lane that runs the Gradle `test` task, which executes the unit tests of every build variant.

nodes.name: bump_version_code_and_push
nodes.summary: Lane that increments the versionCode, commits app/build.gradle with a version bump message, and pushes the commit to the git remote.

nodes.name: firebase_beta
nodes.summary: Lane that bumps, commits and pushes the versionCode, builds the Beta variant with `clean assembleBeta`, uploads it to Firebase App Distribution for the tester group, and posts the build number to two Slack webhooks.

nodes.name: deploy
nodes.summary: Lane that bumps and commits the versionCode with a Play Store release message, builds the release APK with `clean assembleRelease`, and uploads it to Google Play; the git tag step is commented out.

nodes.name: bump_version_code
nodes.summary: Lane that reads ../app/build.gradle, finds the number after `versionCode` with a regex, writes that number plus one back to the file, and returns the new code for the release lanes to put in their commit messages.

nodes.name: Pluginfile
nodes.summary: Fastlane plugin manifest that adds the `fastlane-plugin-firebase_app_distribution` gem, which supplies the upload action that the firebase_beta lane uses.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Auto-generated fastlane documentation that lists the five Android lanes (test, bump_version_code_and_push, firebase_beta, deploy, bump_version_code) with their `fastlane android` commands and one-line descriptions, plus install pointers. Fastlane rewrites it on every run.

nodes.name: libs.versions.toml
nodes.summary: Gradle version catalog for the whole build: SDK levels (compile 37, min 23, target 36), plugin versions (AGP 9.1.1, Kotlin 2.3.20, KSP, Spotless, ktlint, detekt), library coordinates for AndroidX, Compose with Navigation 3, Room, Retrofit, OkHttp, the AWS S3 SDK, CameraX, Koin, Firebase, MapLibre and test tools, and bundles for compose, camerax, koin, testing and roborazzi.
nodes.languageNotes: TOML version catalog with `version.ref` indirection; comments explain pins such as material-icons-extended at 1.7.8 and activity-compose 1.12+ for Navigation 3 back handling.

nodes.name: gradle-wrapper.properties
nodes.summary: Gradle wrapper settings that pin the build to the Gradle 9.5.1 binary distribution stored under GRADLE_USER_HOME, with a 10 second network timeout, no download retries, and validation of the distribution URL.

nodes.name: gradlew
nodes.summary: Generated POSIX start script for the Gradle wrapper: it resolves its own directory through symlinks, finds Java from JAVA_HOME or PATH, raises the open file limit, converts paths on Cygwin and MSYS, and launches gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar with the JVM options. CI actions and codeAnalysis.sh run every Gradle task through it.
nodes.languageNotes: Avoids bash arrays for strict POSIX sh; it splits JVM option variables with xargs and sed escaping, then rebuilds the argument list with `eval set --`.

nodes.name: warn
nodes.summary: Prints its arguments to stderr as a non-fatal warning, used when the script cannot query or raise the open file descriptor limit.

nodes.name: die
nodes.summary: Prints an error message framed by blank lines to stderr and exits with status 1, used when JAVA_HOME is invalid, java is missing, or xargs is not available.

nodes.name: copyright.kt
nodes.summary: Apache License 2.0 header template with a `$YEAR` placeholder and the Treetracker copyright, which the Spotless `licenseHeaderFile` step in the root build.gradle puts at the top of Kotlin sources.

nodes.name: setSyncOverlay
nodes.summary: Writes an explicit visibility into the private sync overlay StateFlow instead of flipping it. The developer options sync switch calls it with the new switch state.

nodes.name: setSensorOverlay
nodes.summary: Writes an explicit visibility into the private sensor overlay StateFlow instead of flipping it. The developer options sensor switch calls it with the new switch state.

nodes.name: backgroundColor
nodes.summary: Composable ButtonColors override that gives the shadow color when enabled and the disabled shadow color otherwise, wrapped in rememberUpdatedState. TextButton draws the raised shadow layer of a depth button with it.

nodes.name: contentColor
nodes.summary: Composable ButtonColors override that gives the face color when enabled and the disabled face color otherwise, wrapped in rememberUpdatedState. TextButton paints the top face of a depth button with it.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Value equality for DepthButtonColors. It is true for the same instance, false for null or another class, and otherwise compares shadowColor, color, disabledShadowColor and disabledColor in turn.

nodes.name: hashCode
nodes.summary: Folds the hash codes of the four colors with the 31 multiplier, in the same field order as equals, so DepthButtonColors instances that compare equal also share a hash code.

layers.name: App Shell and Navigation
layers.description: Application and activity entry points, the root composable host, Koin dependency wiring, and the Navigation 3 routes and org-configured flow controllers that connect every screen.

layers.name: Feature Screens
layers.description: Jetpack Compose screens and their view models for each grower-facing feature, such as sign-up, user and wallet selection, tree capture and review, dashboard, map, messaging, surveys, settings, and developer options.

layers.name: UI Foundation and Resources
layers.description: Shared Compose components, dialogs, colors and themes, the base view model with its one-shot UI event and snackbar plumbing, and the Android drawable, string, and XML resources.

layers.name: Domain Logic and Sync
layers.description: Domain models, repositories, and use cases for growers, organizations, sessions, and tree captures, including GPS convergence, capture and setup flow scopes, and the uploaders and WorkManager worker that sync data to the backend API.

layers.name: Data Sources
layers.description: Local and remote data access: the Room databases with their DAOs, entities, migrations, and exported schema versions, the typed SharedPreferences wrapper, the S3 object storage client, and the Retrofit services and request and response models for the backend API.

layers.name: Shared Utilities and Telemetry
layers.description: Cross-cutting helpers for images, time, GPS, validation, coroutines, and state updates, together with the Firebase Analytics and Crashlytics wrappers that many layers call.

layers.name: Unit and UI Tests
layers.description: JVM unit tests that mirror the main packages, Robolectric Compose UI tests, Roborazzi screenshot tests, shared test rules and fakes, and the debug-only tests of the agent app functions.

layers.name: E2E and Agent Tooling
layers.description: Device-level test tooling: the Test Buddy flow suite and its run, seed, and CI helper scripts, the screen tour, the debug-only E2E activity and AppFunctions that let agents seed growers and trees, and the Claude Code skills with their evals.

layers.name: Build, CI and Release
layers.description: Gradle build scripts and version catalog, lint and formatting configs, Firebase and ProGuard module settings, secret decryption, fastlane release lanes, GitHub Actions workflows for build, test, E2E, and store deployment, and repository governance files.

layers.name: Documentation
layers.description: Project README and contributor docs, engineering, product, testing, and release guides, and the numbered task records with their attached test reports.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Treetracker Android is the field data collection tool of Greenstand's Treetracker platform: growers capture tree photos with GPS locations, and the app moves that data on toward verification. The README covers project setup with the dev build variant and QC releases through Firebase App Distribution, and the project overview frames the goal of verifiable tree records that support climate restoration and income for tree growers. The user stories list the field constraints that shape the design you will see in later steps: offline use, battery life, GPS reliance, poor connectivity, low literacy and shared devices.

tour.title: Architecture and Docs Map
tour.description: The architecture guide describes an MVVM design: each screen has a view model built on BaseViewModel with a typed Action sealed class, and a stateful Root composable wraps a stateless UI composable that previews and Roborazzi snapshot tests target. It also names the three Koin modules (AppModule, RoomModule, NetworkModule) and the core stack of Jetpack Compose, Room, Retrofit, AWS S3 object storage, CameraX, coroutines and Firebase. The package structure page maps these ideas to the packages under org.greenstand.android.TreeTracker, and the root CLAUDE.md (titled AGENTS.md) is the table of contents for the whole docs tree and the per-task workflow.
tour.languageLesson: A Kotlin sealed class restricts a type to a closed set of subclasses. When user actions are modeled as a sealed Action class, the compiler can check that a `when` expression handles every action, which makes this a common way to model UI events in MVVM.

tour.title: App Startup and Entry Points
tour.description: An Android app has no main function, so start with the manifest: it declares TreeTrackerApplication, the single-task TreeTrackerActivity launcher with its org deep link filter, ImageCaptureActivity, and a data-sync foreground service for WorkManager. TreeTrackerApplication runs first and initializes Firebase, the object storage client and the Koin dependency graph. TreeTrackerActivity then parses the start route from the launch intent and composes Root inside CustomTheme, or shows a no-GPS dialog on a device without a GPS provider.
tour.languageLesson: Android creates the Application subclass named in AndroidManifest.xml once per process, before any activity. That makes it the right place for process-wide setup, such as starting a dependency injection container, while activities only host UI.

tour.title: Dependency Wiring with Koin
tour.description: The Koin graph that TreeTrackerApplication starts in Step 3 lives in three modules. AppModule has the widest reach of any source file: it wires 18 ViewModels, the repositories, uploaders and use cases, Android system services, and scoped bindings for the capture setup and capture flows, so a dependency walk from it reaches most of the domain and feature code. RoomModule registers AppDatabase with each DAO plus a separate MessageDatabase, and NetworkModule provides the Retrofit instance and the messaging API service. Use AppModule as an index, because almost every class later in this tour is constructed there.
tour.languageLesson: Koin is a Kotlin dependency injection library configured with a DSL instead of annotation processing. `single` defines one shared instance, `factory` creates a new instance for every request, `viewModel` ties an instance to the Android ViewModel lifecycle, and a `scope` block defines objects that live only while a named scope is open.

tour.title: Compose Root and Navigation
tour.description: Root is the top-level composable that TreeTrackerActivity shows: it provides the ViewModel factory and snackbar controller as CompositionLocals and re-hydrates the current organization before it renders Host. Host keeps a saveable Navigation 3 back stack and maps every typed route key from Routes.kt to its screen composable, so it links directly to almost every screen in the app. Navigator wraps the back stack with push, pop and throttled variants that block double-tap navigation, and RouteRegistry translates route strings from organization config JSON into typed keys, which the configurable flows in later steps depend on.
tour.languageLesson: Navigation 3 treats the back stack as a plain list of keys that the app owns. Marking route keys with @Serializable (data objects for screens without arguments, data classes for screens that need ids or flags) lets that list be saved and restored. A CompositionLocal such as LocalNavigator passes a value down the composable tree without adding a parameter to every function.

tour.title: Screen Building Blocks
tour.description: Every screen reuses a small shared foundation. BaseViewModel holds UI state in a StateFlow and delivers one-shot events through a replaying SharedFlow, CustomTheme provides the Montserrat text styles and brand colors, and TestTags is the most depended-upon file in the graph because screens, UI tests and end-to-end flows all use its tags. The home dashboard shows the pattern at work: DashboardScreen shows synced and pending tree counts with buttons to upload, open messages, start tracking and open settings, and DashboardViewModel observes the counts from Room and starts or cancels the unique WorkManager sync.
tour.languageLesson: A Kotlin StateFlow always holds a current value, which fits screen state that the UI redraws from. A SharedFlow suits events that must be handled once, such as a snackbar or a navigation command. Wrapping each event in a consumable holder stops a replayed event from being handled a second time.

tour.title: Growers and Organizations
tour.description: Two domain concepts shape most flows: a User is a grower account with a wallet, tree count, names, photo and power-user flag, and an organization defines the theme, features and flow steps on the device. At launch, SplashScreenViewModel saves the device config, resolves an org link from a deep link or the Play install referrer, and applies the org config that OrgConfigProvider fetches from Firebase Remote Config. OrgRepo persists the current org, seeds the default Greenstand org and drops unknown flow routes, and the org links design note explains the goal: fewer per-org app flavors and no manual org entry.

tour.title: Capture Setup Flow
tour.description: Before a grower captures trees, the capture setup flow collects who is planting and which wallet receives the trees; the navigation flows page maps it next to the signup, capture and messaging flows. CaptureSetupNavigationController walks the org-configured setup steps, guards against double taps, and starts the session, sensors and GPS before it hands over to tree capture. SetupScope is a Koin scope that lives for one setup run and shares CaptureSetupData (user, destination wallet, session note, org name) with every setup screen, and SessionTracker turns that data into a capture session and restores it if Android killed the app.
tour.languageLesson: Android can kill a background app process and later recreate it at the last screen. Saveable state such as a Navigation 3 back stack comes back, but in-memory objects such as a Koin scope do not, so the app must save key ids (for example in preferences) and rebuild those objects on restore.

tour.title: GPS Convergence
tour.description: Verifiable tree records depend on good locations, so the app waits for the GPS position to settle before it accepts a capture. The Add Tree flow page describes this convergence gate: a progress indicator runs until recent location samples converge, or until a timeout lets capture go ahead anyway. LocationDataCapturer keeps a sliding window of recent fixes and judges convergence against thresholds from ConvergenceConfiguration, while Convergence computes the mean, variance and standard deviation of latitude and longitude incrementally as the window slides. LocationDataCapturer also stores every fix of the session as location data for the sync step later in the tour.

tour.title: Tree Capture Flow
tour.description: This is the core of the app and the most tightly coupled group of files in the graph. TreeCaptureScreen shows the rear camera preview, and TreeCaptureViewModel pins a GPS location from Step 9 and waits up to 30 seconds for it before it accepts a photo and hands it to TreeCapturer. TreeCapturer builds the tree record with the photo, step counts and rotation matrix, keeps every change in PendingTreeStore, and saves the tree through CreateTreeUseCase. CaptureFlowNavigationController moves through the org-defined capture steps and loops back to the camera after each saved tree, and CaptureFlowScope holds these per-flow objects and can reopen at a restored screen after process death.

tour.title: Local Storage with Room
tour.description: The app is built for offline use, so every capture lands in local storage first. AppDatabase is the Room database at schema version 9, and it keeps the legacy v1 planter and tree_capture entities next to the v2 session, user, tree, location, device config and organization entities. TreeTrackerDAO, the second most imported source file, is the aggregate DAO with about ninety queries for upload queues, upload flags, counts and Flow streams, and TreeEntity is one v2 tree row with its session link, photo path, coordinates and upload state. The exported 9.json schema shows the organization table that stores the org flow definitions from Step 7, and Preferences wraps SharedPreferences with typed keys for smaller state.
tour.languageLesson: Room generates the SQLite code for @Database, @Entity and @Dao declarations at compile time. An exported JSON schema for each version gives a reviewable history of the database. Room can derive simple upgrades as auto migrations from two exported schemas, while complex changes still need hand-written Migration objects.

tour.title: Background Sync to the Backend
tour.description: When the grower taps upload on the dashboard from Step 6, the app runs TreeSyncWorker, a WorkManager job that runs as a foreground data-sync service and shows upload progress in a notification. The worker calls SyncDataUseCase, which uploads in a fixed order: messages, device config, users, sessions, legacy trees, trees, then GPS locations. The data sync architecture page gives the shared uploader recipe that TreeUploader follows: upload photos, upload a JSON bundle through ObjectStorageClient to object storage, mark the rows as uploaded, and delete local photos. TreeUploader works in windows of 50 trees and builds legacy V1 or V2 bundles, which is why both database generations from Step 11 still matter.
tour.languageLesson: WorkManager runs background work that must finish even when the user leaves the app. A CoroutineWorker does its work in a suspend function, and running it as a foreground service with a notification lets a long upload continue. Enqueuing it as unique work keeps only one sync with that name active at a time.

tour.title: Build Variants and Feature Flags
tour.description: Several behaviors from earlier steps depend on the build variant. app/build.gradle defines the release, prerelease, debug, beta and dev build types and injects per-variant BuildConfig fields such as the API gateway, object storage buckets and feature flags, and the build variants page explains the differences: relaxed accuracy for dev, blur detection in debug, the test environment for beta, and production endpoints with minification for release. FeatureFlags reads those BuildConfig values to switch tree height, tree note, DBH, automatic sign-out, blur detection and org links. The version catalog in libs.versions.toml pins every SDK level, plugin and library, including Compose with Navigation 3, Room, Koin, CameraX and the AWS S3 SDK.
tour.languageLesson: A Gradle version catalog (libs.versions.toml) keeps versions and library coordinates in one TOML file, and build scripts refer to them through typed accessors such as `libs.<alias>`. A build type can add `buildConfigField` entries, which Gradle compiles into a generated BuildConfig class that Kotlin code reads as constants.

tour.title: Unit and UI Tests
tour.description: The testing guide describes four test layers: JVM unit tests with MockK, Turbine and a coroutine rule, Robolectric Compose UI tests, end-to-end flows, and Roborazzi screenshot tests. MainCoroutineRule and ComposeUiTest are among the most depended-upon files in the graph because dozens of tests build on them: the rule swaps Dispatchers.Main for a test dispatcher, and the base class gives each UI test a real Navigator over an inspectable back stack, plus theme and Koin wiring. KoinGraphTest starts the real appModule, roomModule and networkModule from Step 4 and checks that every definition and capture scope resolves, so wiring mistakes fail in tests instead of at runtime.
tour.languageLesson: Robolectric runs Android framework code on the plain JVM, so Compose UI tests run without an emulator. A JUnit rule that replaces Dispatchers.Main with a test dispatcher makes coroutines launched from a view model run predictably inside a test.

tour.title: End-to-End Flows and CI
tour.description: End-to-end flows drive the real debug app on an emulator by tapping the TestTags resource ids from Step 6. The e2e README lists the flow families (signup, capture, settings, sad-path, org-config, dev-tools, known-bug), run.sh runs the whole suite on one disposable emulator, and the shared signup.yaml subflow takes a fresh install to the dashboard so that most flows start with a real grower account. On GitHub Actions, pull_request.yml runs code analysis, unit tests with a debug build, and Roborazzi screenshot checks as parallel jobs, and the required android-e2e.yml check runs every flow through run.sh on an emulator.
tour.languageLesson: In GitHub Actions, the `on` key sets the triggers, each entry under `jobs` runs in parallel on its own runner by default, and the `steps` inside a job run in order. A reusable workflow called through `workflow_call` lets several pipelines share one build definition.
